## 10.0 Method, Status Rules and Limitations

### 10.0.1 Method

1. Targets: each of the 84 WA leaf items from the Part 1 checklist got three queries. The first was an official query limited to support.microsoft.com and learn.microsoft.com. The second, where relevant, was a developer-documentation query on learn.microsoft.com. The third was an independent query that excluded Microsoft domains.
2. Fetch and extraction: the top official hit, the top developer hit and the top two independent hits were fetched in full. A structured extraction then recorded entry points, UI elements, interactions, shortcuts, conditions, confirmations and errors, Windows 10/7 differences and developer APIs. Labels were kept verbatim, and a default was recorded only when the page states one.
3. Retry: 12 targets whose official hit was irrelevant were retried against up to three alternative official pages.
4. Anchors: four cross-cutting pages were read in full. These were the [26H2 What's new for IT pros](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) page, the [Insider blog post on taskbar and Start](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/), the [File Explorer support article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/file-explorer-in-windows-ef370130-1cca-9dc5-e0df-2f7416fe1cb1) and the [keyboard shortcuts article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/keyboard-shortcuts-in-windows-dcc61a57-8ff0-cffe-9796-cb9706c75eec). The shortcut article was parsed from its HTML because its Windows-key glyph is an image and is lost in plain-text extraction.
5. Legacy differences: Microsoft's [Windows 11 specifications page](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-11-specifications), Wikipedia's [list of features removed in Windows 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_features_removed_in_Windows_11) and others were extracted into Appendix 3B.

### 10.0.2 Evidence tiers used in this chapter

T1 = Microsoft documentation, support articles and official blogs. T2 = source code or official repositories. T4 = independent press, tutorials, OEM pages and videos. T5 = community Q&A and forums, including Microsoft Q&A at learn.microsoft.com/answers, which is T5 even though it sits on a Microsoft domain. Under the Part 1 rubric, T5 is never the only support for a material claim.

### 10.0.3 Status rules applied

- COMPLETE: an official source enumerates the item fully. Only WA.09.06 (Windows key + arrow shortcuts) qualifies, and its live-build check is still pending (VP-03).
- PARTIAL (official): at least one T1/T2 source describes the item, but it is not specific to build 26300.9711 and full coverage on the live shell is unproven.
- PARTIAL (independent only): only T4/T5 evidence exists. The affected items are WA.01.02, WA.13.10, WA.13.11, WA.13.13, WA.13.18 and WA.16, all flagged in Section 10.18.
- NOT APPLICABLE: WA.08.04 Timeline, which is not part of Windows 11.

### 10.0.4 Limitations

- L-01: Extraction was LLM-assisted. Element rows are what the source says, not observations of a live system. Re-read the cited page before quoting any label as a Windows UI string.
- L-02: Microsoft support articles are evergreen and often lag behind the shipping build. Section 10.18 lists the specific conflicts found.
- L-03: Independent sources describe preview or rollout states that may differ from what 26H2 GA shows on a given device, because Microsoft uses controlled feature rollout.
- L-04: A "—" in the default column means no default was stated. It does not mean the feature has no default.
- L-05: No visual measurements (sizes, radii, timings) are recorded in this chapter. Those belong to Part 4 (WC tokens) and will be tagged MEASURED or ESTIMATE.

## 10.1 26H2 Shell Delta (verified against official 26H2 sources)

Facts in this section come from full reads of the official [26H2 What's new](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) page (updated 2026-09-29) and the [Insider blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/) (2026-05-15). Insider-blog statements describe the Experimental channel at the time of posting and are marked "preview-scoped".

| ID | Area | Change | Scope / condition | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D26.01 | Start | Redesigned Start with a scrollable All section, category and grid views, and a responsive layout. Users choose a Start size and can show or hide the Pinned, Recent and All sections independently. | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.02 | Start | Section toggles for Pinned, Recommended and All; file recommendations controlled separately from File Explorer recents; Start size Small or Large; option to hide name and profile picture; "Recommended" renamed "Recent". | Preview-scoped (Experimental channel, May 2026) | [Insider blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/) |
| D26.03 | Taskbar | Taskbar can sit at the bottom, top, left or right. A smaller taskbar option reduces icon size and taskbar height. | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.04 | Taskbar | Position setting is in Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors. Vertical positions align icons top or centered; horizontal positions align left or centered. Start, Search and flyouts open relative to the taskbar edge. Auto-hide, the tablet-optimized taskbar, touch gestures and search boxes were not yet supported in alternate positions. | Preview-scoped; GA status of these limits unverified (GAP-B2-01) | [Insider blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/) |
| D26.05 | Taskbar | "Show smaller taskbar buttons" set to Always makes both icons and taskbar height smaller; no restart or sign-out required. | Preview-scoped | [Insider blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/) |
| D26.06 | Taskbar | Monitoring of supported AI agents from the taskbar; Researcher in Microsoft Copilot is the first supported experience; progress shown on the taskbar and a notification when work completes. | GA 26H2; Researcher requires Microsoft 365 Copilot | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.07 | Taskbar | App-specific taskbar actions enabled by default for commercial devices. | Commercial devices | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.08 | File Explorer | AI actions to edit supported images or summarize documents. The Summarize action in Copilot covers OneDrive and SharePoint files and needs a Microsoft 365 subscription and Copilot licence. | Licence-dependent | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.09 | File Explorer | Hover quick actions Open file location and Ask Copilot on File Explorer Home. | Work or school account | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.10 | File Explorer | Additional archive formats: `uu`, `cpio`, `xar`, NuGet (`nupkg`). | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.11 | File Explorer | View and Sort preferences preserved in folders such as Downloads and Documents when apps open File Explorer directly to them; voice typing when renaming a file; faster Home launch. | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.12 | Search | Preview results without opening the item; typo-tolerant app search; clearer labels for app, setting, file, web result or Store suggestion; automatic indexing of frequently used folders (managed in Settings > Privacy & security > Search). | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.13 | Security | Administrator protection: just-in-time admin privileges with profile separation; off by default, enabled through Intune or Group Policy. | Managed enablement | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.14 | Sign-in | Plugin credential managers for passkeys; PIN setup for security keys during authentication; Enhanced Sign-in Security with compatible peripheral fingerprint sensors. | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.15 | Update / session | Eligible updates install together with the monthly security update; a device manually put to sleep returns to sleep after an update, even when automatic sleep is Never. | GA 26H2 | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |
| D26.16 | OOBE | Autopilot device preparation device association adds setup customization during OOBE; first sign-in restore of settings and the Store app list for Entra hybrid joined, Cloud PC and multi-user devices. | Managed devices | [What's new 26H2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-26h2) |

| WA.01.01.i22 | Open Settings, select Personalization, then select Background. | The background options page opens. | T4 | [geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/) |
| WA.01.01.i23 | Open the Personalize your background menu and select Windows spotlight. | The desktop switches to the current Spotlight picture; new images download and display automatically, with a fresh one each day. | T4 | [geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/) |

| WA.01.01.i25 | Select Slideshow, then click Browse next to Choose a folder for your slideshow. | A folder picker opens. | T4 | [geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/) |

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- For multiple displays, Picture can use the same picture on all displays or a different picture on each display. This option is not available when using multiple desktops. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- With Slideshow on multiple displays, each screen displays a different picture from the selected folder. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- With multiple desktops, a different background picture can be selected for each desktop. Configuring a background picture per monitor is not supported, and Slideshow is not supported. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- The wording or display of folder-selection controls and the available interval choices may vary by Windows 11 release, language, device configuration, or organizational policy. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A work or school PC may expose different background or Spotlight controls because of organizational management or policy; edition and policy requirements can apply to managed deployments. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Microsoft documents that slideshow backgrounds are not supported with multiple virtual desktops. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Windows 11 can show different slideshow images on multiple physical monitors; the page cautions that displays may not advance in perfect synchrony. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A local slideshow can use images already stored on the computer. Windows Spotlight needs connectivity to obtain fresh content. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Sleep, hibernation, power-saving behavior, disconnected storage, or policy restrictions can affect what is seen or when a wallpaper changes. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Windows Spotlight needs an internet connection to fetch new pictures. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Spotlight works the same on Windows Home and Pro. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- On a work PC managed by an organization, an administrator may turn Spotlight off. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page states no confirmation dialog for changing wallpaper settings. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If the slideshow is not changing, check that Slideshow is selected, that the selected folder exists and contains image files, and that local files work. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A disconnected network location or removable drive can prevent Windows from retrieving a slideshow image. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If Slideshow is missing, confirm that Background—not Lock screen—is open; organizational management, Windows updates, or device configuration may affect the available controls. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page advises against applying registry edits copied from unrelated Windows versions because there is no universally valid registry fix for a missing Slideshow control. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If Spotlight is disabled by an organization administrator, its option may be missing or greyed out. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If a slideshow picture does not change right away, wait for one full interval. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If a slideshow stops changing or resets to one picture, check whether a new theme replaced the slideshow setting, whether the slideshow folder was moved, renamed, or deleted, whether the PC is on battery or the power plan has paused the slideshow, and whether a work or school policy controls the background. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings → Personalization → Background ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings → Personalization → Lock screen ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/automatically-change-desktop-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings › Personalization › Background ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings › Personalization ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-automatically-change-desktop-background-wallpaper-in-windows-11/), T4)

- `Ctrl + mouse wheel` — Resize desktop icons. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/answers/questions/5891333/todays-windows-11-update-messed-up-my-desktop-icon), T5)
- `Win+R` — Opens the Run dialog to start Registry Editor by entering `regedit`. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page says that icons moving on their own, especially with multiple monitors and Copilot in Windows (in preview) enabled, is a known issue in Windows 11 23H2. It says Copilot might be disabled automatically on multi-monitor setups until a fix from newer cumulative updates is installed. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/answers/questions/5891333/todays-windows-11-update-messed-up-my-desktop-icon), T5)
- Display-resolution changes, such as docking or undocking a laptop, can cause Windows to re-flow the icon grid. ([winresolve.com](https://winresolve.com/managing-desktop-icons-shortcuts-windows11/), T4)
- The context-menu method works on Windows 11 Home and Pro, needs no administrator rights, and applies immediately without a restart. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The Registry Editor method requires an administrator account and a restart for the change to take effect. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page states no hardware, region, Insider, or rollout restrictions. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- A checkmark beside Auto arrange icons means it is on; no checkmark means it is off. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A checkmark beside Align icons to grid means it is on. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If no desktop icons are visible, the page says to check Show desktop icons in View. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page warns that an incorrect registry edit can cause problems elsewhere in Windows and recommends exporting a backup first. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-turn-on-or-off-auto-arrange-icons-on-desktop-in-windows-11/), T4)

| WA.01.03.i08 | Choose Show more options. | This is for inspecting legacy context-menu extensions; the documented IExplorerCommand command appears in the Windows 11 context menu. | T1 | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| WA.01.03.i09 | Right-click | Opens the context menu. | T4 | [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/) |
| WA.01.03.i10 | Click Show more options | Opens the legacy, Windows 10-style context menu. | T4 | [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/) |
| WA.01.03.i11 | Turn on Show more options in settings | Enables access to the legacy context menu; no settings path is specified. | T4 | [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Shift + F10` — Opens the context menu for the selected item; in File Explorer, the simplified menu appears first. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6033728/right-click), T5)
- `Shift + Menu key` — Opens the classic full menu from the simplified menu. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6033728/right-click), T5)
- `Shift+right-click` — Shows the Show more options context menu; requires a mouse. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6033728/right-click), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Applies to packaged desktop apps and unpackaged Win32 apps that use a sparse package. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer), T1)
- The DLL architecture must match the File Explorer architecture that loads it. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer), T1)
- If the command does not appear after installing or updating a package, restart File Explorer or sign out and back in so the shell reloads the extension registration. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer), T1)
- The legacy menu may still be needed by third-party apps with extensions that rely on it. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/), T4)
- Microsoft says it is publishing guidance to help developers migrate extensions to the modern context menu. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Use Show more options only to inspect legacy context-menu extensions. The documented windows.fileExplorerContextMenus and IExplorerCommand command appears in the Windows 11 context menu. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer), T1)
- A file type association can make an app available in Open with or add an editing verb for a file type, but it does not provide the general-purpose context menu extension described in the article. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer), T1)
- The legacy context menu is described as the Windows 10-style menu and is currently accessible through Show more options. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/), T4)
- Microsoft says it will not remove the legacy context menu while legacy apps and extensions still rely on it. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/), T4)
- The modern context menu is described as having become cluttered and sluggish; Microsoft says it is working to improve its speed and allow customization. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/08/20/will-windows-11-remove-the-windows-10-era-right-click-menu-microsoft-reveals-whats-next/), T4)
- The original context menu was bundled with Windows 10, Windows 8, and Windows 7; in Windows 11 it is available through Show more options. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2021/07/20/microsoft-is-upgrading-right-click-context-menus-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The legacy menu supports rounded corners, but its design remains otherwise unchanged. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2021/07/20/microsoft-is-upgrading-right-click-context-menus-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The article says the classic menu had accumulated commands in an unregulated environment and that commands relying on File Explorer could cause performance and reliability issues on Windows 10 and older versions. It says the new approach loads the classic menu without affecting overall system performance. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2021/07/20/microsoft-is-upgrading-right-click-context-menus-in-windows-11/), T4)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `IExplorerCommand` | Implement in a native COM DLL. The implementation supplies the command title, icon, state, and action. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetTitle` | Supplies the command title. Keep GetTitle fast; do not perform expensive work on the File Explorer UI path. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetIcon` | Supplies the command icon. Keep GetIcon fast; do not perform expensive work on the File Explorer UI path. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetState` | Controls whether the command appears and can be selected. States shown include ECS_HIDDEN, ECS_DISABLED, and ECS_ENABLED. Keep GetState fast; do not perform expensive work on the File Explorer UI path. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::Invoke` | Receives the selected items through IShellItemArray. Use it to enumerate the current selection. Run longer operations after Invoke is called. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetToolTip` | Supplies the command tooltip. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetCanonicalName` | Supplies the command's canonical name. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::GetFlags` | Supplies command flags; the example returns ECF_DEFAULT. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IExplorerCommand::EnumSubCommands` | Supplies child commands for an app-attributed flyout. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IShellItemArray` | Passed to Invoke; use it to enumerate the current selection. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IEnumExplorerCommand` | The output type used by EnumSubCommands to supply child commands. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `IBindCtx` | The second parameter to Invoke in the example implementation. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `windows.comServer` | Manifest extension category that registers the native DLL as a COM server using com:ComServer, com:SurrogateServer, and com:Class. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `com:Class` | Registers the COM class. Its Id is the command CLSID, Path is the package-relative DLL path, and ThreadingModel is set to STA in the example. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |
| `windows.fileExplorerContextMenus` | Manifest extension category for registering the File Explorer context-menu command. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/integrate-packaged-app-with-file-explorer) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Shift + F10` — Opens the context menu for the currently selected item, as an alternative to right-clicking. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The available Category, Grid, and List views depend on the Windows 11 version and the view last selected on the PC. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- The page describes the remembered pinned-section state and remembered app view on supported and updated systems. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- On work or school PCs, organization policies may define or restrict Start layouts; pins or layouts may return after sign-in, restart, or a policy refresh. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Removing a pin from Start removes only the shortcut; it does not delete the app, folder, or folder contents. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- A Start folder containing only one item is removed automatically, and the remaining item returns to the main pinned area. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- A managed layout may restrict customization or reapply pins after they are removed. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- Dropping an item onto a folder may be difficult at first because Windows may treat the attempt as moving the item to a new position. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)
- Folders cannot be dropped onto other folders to create subfolders or merge folders. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)
- A folder cannot be deleted directly; its pinned items must be moved out first. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)
- Each folder displays no more than four pinned icons, even if it contains more pinned items. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 uses pinned tiles rather than the Windows 11 pinned-app grid. The page says Windows 10 tiles can be resized, moved, and grouped into named sections; tiles can also be organized into folders. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-windows-start-menu), T1)
- Windows 11 has moved beyond Windows 10 live-tile workflows: there are no tile sizes to adjust and no tile groups in the old sense. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- The page says folder and grouping functionality was removed in the original Windows 11 release and restored in version 22H2. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)
- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 comparison for this feature is stated. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Start settings > Folders ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/pin-apps-and-websites-in-windows-11-organize-start-and-taskbar.440333/), T5)
- Right-clicking Pinned displays a direct link to the Start Menu settings in the preferences app. ([ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2022/08/18/windows-11-version-22h2-start-menu-changes/), T4)

- In the previous Start menu, users had to click “All apps” to find the installed-app list on a separate page; the new menu puts “All” on the main screen. ([bleepingcomputer.com](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/how-to-use-the-new-windows-11-start-menu-now-rolling-out/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page does not state any SKU, hardware, region, or rollout conditions. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Personalization/customize-the-windows-start-menu), T1)
- The page does not identify this behavior as a 26H2 feature or provide a build/channel. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Personalization/customize-the-windows-start-menu), T1)
- These features were already rolling out before the 26H2 release; Microsoft said they would roll out to more users starting with 26H2. The page says rollout is gradual. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZDGM69Q68Ik&xstg=CAMSBhUD_LL2Hw==), T4)
- The video’s size comparison mentions a 100% DPI setting and a larger display. No eligibility requirements by SKU, region, or hardware are stated. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZDGM69Q68Ik&xstg=CAMSBhUD_LL2Hw==), T4)
- The narrator says the redesigned Start menu is not new and that most users probably already have it; the additional settings may be new to them. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63Pf51WuUbo), T4)
- Windows features are released through controlled rollouts, so not everyone receives them at the same time; the major update enables most of them. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63Pf51WuUbo), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page describes Start resizing and full-screen options in its Windows 10 content; it does not state Windows 11 Start menu size controls. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Personalization/customize-the-windows-start-menu), T1)
- The previous version had Pinned and Recommended; the redesigned Start menu replaces Recommended with Recent and All. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63Pf51WuUbo), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings (the page does not provide a specific path for toggling recommended providers). ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Personalization/customize-the-windows-start-menu), T1)
- Settings > Personalization > Start ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63Pf51WuUbo), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + X` — Opens the menu from which you can select Shut down or sign out > Hibernate. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- `CTRL+ALT+DEL` — Shows the Windows Security dialog box. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/start/policy-settings?tabs=start&pivots=windows-11), T1)
- `WIN` — Open Start Menu ([helpcenter.ccac.edu](https://helpcenter.ccac.edu/microsoft-windows/windows-11-guide), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Hibernate might not be available on all PCs; the page gives PCs with InstantGo as an example. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- The account and power policies shown in the article use CSP paths under Device or User policy scope, as specified in the individual paths. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/start/policy-settings?tabs=start&pivots=windows-11), T1)
- The page lists GPO support for Disable Account Notifications, Hide Sign out, and Hide entry points for Fast User Switching. The other listed account and power menu policies are marked as having no GPO path. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/start/policy-settings?tabs=start&pivots=windows-11), T1)
- The page states that Hide entry points for Fast User Switching affects entry points on the sign-in screen, Start menu, and Task Manager. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/start/policy-settings?tabs=start&pivots=windows-11), T1)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + Ctrl + D` — Add a desktop. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Shift + Right arrow` — Move an app to a monitor on the right. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Shift + Left arrow` — Move an app to a monitor on the left. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Tab` — Show all open apps and view additional desktops you've created. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Ctrl + Right arrow` — Switch between desktops you've created on the right. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Ctrl + Left arrow` — Switch between desktops you've created on the left. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Ctrl + F4` — Close the desktop you're using. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key` — Displays the Start menu and moves the cursor to the search box. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Ctrl + escape` — Displays the Start menu. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Windows Key + D` — Minimises all programs and displays the desktop. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Windows Key + M` — Minimises all open programs. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Windows Key + E` — Opens a new explorer window. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Windows Key + F` — Displays the Windows search dialog box. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `Windows Key + U` — Displays the Windows utility manager dialog box for controlling accessibility options. ([abilitynet.org.uk](https://abilitynet.org.uk/factsheets/keyboard-shortcuts), T4)
- `WINDOWS KEY` — Opens the Start menu. ([bva.org](https://bva.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/An-Introduction-to-Windows-11-and-JAWS-Resource-File.docx), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- In previous Windows versions, the Search box was anchored at the bottom of the Start menu; in Windows 11 it is at the top. ([bva.org](https://bva.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/An-Introduction-to-Windows-11-and-JAWS-Resource-File.docx), T4)
- The Recommended List replaces the Windows Timeline in previous versions, which displayed running apps and past activities. ([bva.org](https://bva.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/An-Introduction-to-Windows-11-and-JAWS-Resource-File.docx), T4)
- The Start menu and Taskbar can be moved to the left or right, but the Taskbar can no longer be relocated to the top of the screen. ([bva.org](https://bva.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/An-Introduction-to-Windows-11-and-JAWS-Resource-File.docx), T4)


## 10.4 WA.03 — Taskbar

### WA.03.01 Taskbar alignment and position (center/left; top/left/right in 26H2)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | PARTIAL — 1 T1/T2 and 2 T4/T5 sources relevant. Official sources are not specific to build 26300.9711; live-build check pending. |
| Applies to (as stated by sources) | Windows 11 (not build-specific); Windows 11 Insider Preview builds 26100.9267/26200.9267. The article says Release Preview ; Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2; the page says the setting is rolling out gradually. It  |
| Relevant sources | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows) (T1), [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar) (T4), [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/) (T5) |
| Inspected, not relevant | 0 |
| Snippet-only candidates | 9 (register only) |

Entry points:

- Right-click the taskbar and select Taskbar settings. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors > Taskbar position — [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar)
- Right-click an empty spot on the taskbar > Taskbar settings > Taskbar behaviors > Taskbar position — [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/)

The page does not describe a center/left taskbar-alignment setting. | Bottom, top, left, or right | — | T4 | [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar) +1 |

| ID | Input | Result | Tier | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| WA.03.01.i04 | Choose Bottom, Top, Left, or Right under Taskbar position. | The taskbar moves immediately; Start and Search open from its new edge. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/) |

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The position choices are described for Insider Preview builds 26100.9267/26200.9267. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar), T4)
- Release Preview Channel Insiders can use the feature now; the wider release is expected with September Patch Tuesday if testing goes well. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar), T4)
- The feature is rolling out gradually. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar), T4)
- Search box and smaller taskbar support is limited to top and bottom positions. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar), T4)
- No SKU, hardware, or region requirements are stated. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/windows-11-is-dangerously-close-to-letting-you-move-the-taskbar), T4)
- The setting was added to Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2 through updates, but is in a gradual rollout and may not appear on every fully updated PC immediately. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/), T5)
- The page says the tablet-optimized taskbar did not work in alternate positions in the initial rollout, touch gestures were still in progress, and search boxes on other edges collapsed to an icon. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/), T5)
- The page reports conflicting information about whether auto-hide works in alternate positions. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If Taskbar position is absent, the page says the PC may not yet have received the staged rollout. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page states that in Windows 11 the taskbar is positioned at the bottom and has no settings for moving it to the top or side of the screen. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- The Windows 10 section states that the taskbar location can be set to Left, Top, Right, or Bottom under Taskbar location on screen. It says the taskbar must be unlocked before changing its location. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- Windows 10 allowed the taskbar to be placed on any screen edge; Windows 11 initially removed that option. The page describes the traditional Windows 11 taskbar as bottom-aligned and centered. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-taskbar-position-smaller-icons-start-menu-and-run-dialog-whats-actually-available.446849/), T5)

- Rolling out to Windows Insiders in the Experimental channel; the article says the experience is rolling out today. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/), T1)
- No SKU, hardware, or region condition is stated. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/05/15/improving-windows-quality-making-taskbar-and-start-more-personal/), T1)
- The feature is starting to roll out to Windows Insiders in the Canary Channel; the page does not state that it is available to all Insiders. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2025/07/11/announcing-windows-11-insider-preview-build-27898-canary-channel/), T1)
- The new Taskbar size setting is described as being in a recent Windows update available only to testers. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/29/windows-11-gets-two-ways-to-shrink-taskbar-size-which-windows-10-never-had/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Earlier versions of the operating system had a “Use small Taskbar buttons” setting, which disappeared when Windows 11 launched. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-use-smaller-icons-in-the-taskbar-for-windows-11), T4)
- In older versions, enabling small icons also reduced the Taskbar's height. In Windows 11, only the icon size changes and the Taskbar remains the same height. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-use-smaller-icons-in-the-taskbar-for-windows-11), T4)
- Windows 10 had a toggle to change the taskbar size; the page calls its simpler toggle use small taskbar buttons. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/29/windows-11-gets-two-ways-to-shrink-taskbar-size-which-windows-10-never-had/), T4)
- The older Windows 11 smaller-icons option changes icons only, unlike the new setting that changes the taskbar itself. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/29/windows-11-gets-two-ways-to-shrink-taskbar-size-which-windows-10-never-had/), T4)

- Taskbar settings > Taskbar behaviors > Show smaller taskbar buttons ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2025/07/11/announcing-windows-11-insider-preview-build-27898-canary-channel/), T1)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows + I` — Opens Settings; the article directs users to Personalization > Start to change the recent-items setting. ([geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/how-to-view-recent-files-in-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The JumpList API requires package identity. It works in packaged (MSIX) apps and apps packaged with external location, but is not available in unpackaged apps. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list), T1)
- The app must target Windows 10, version 1607 (Anniversary Update, build 14393) or later. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list), T1)
- Jump Lists are app-specific; right-clicking Word shows Word documents, while right-clicking Excel shows spreadsheets. ([geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/how-to-view-recent-files-in-windows-11/), T4)
- An app may have an empty Jump List if it does not support Jump Lists or if recent item tracking is turned off. ([geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/how-to-view-recent-files-in-windows-11/), T4)
- On a work- or school-managed PC, an administrator may disable recent file tracking; the setting may be grayed out. ([geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/how-to-view-recent-files-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The article says the number of recent files and programs visible in jump lists changed starting with Windows 11 version 22H2, but gives no specific limit. ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)
- The article says Group Policy control is available in Windows 11 Pro, Enterprise, and similar editions. ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If the general recent-items setting is disabled, jump lists are emptied. ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)
- An enabled Group Policy can override manual settings. ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The article says jump lists exist in both Windows 10 and Windows 11. ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Personalization > Start ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows?nochrome=), T1)
- Settings > Personalization > Home > “Show recently opened items in Start, shortcut lists, and File Explorer” ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)
- Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Start Menu and Taskbar > “Do not save a history of recently opened documents” ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)
- User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Start Menu and Taskbar > “Do not save a history of recently opened documents” ([w11.es](https://w11.es/en/Tutorials/Recent-files-in-Windows-11:-View--hide--and-manage-them/), T4)

| `JumpListItem.CreateWithArguments` | Creates a jump-list item with an argument string and a display name. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |
| `JumpList.SaveAsync` | Saves changes to the jump list. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |
| `JumpList.Items` | Collection to which items are added; clear it to remove all items the app added. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |
| `JumpListItem.GroupName` | An empty value places an item in the built-in Tasks section; a non-empty value groups it under the named heading. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |
| `JumpListItem.Description` | Sets the item's description. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |

| `Activation arguments` | The app can read the argument string supplied for a selected task at startup. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/jump-list) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win + R` — Opens the Run dialog; the page says to enter `sysdm.cpl`. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- `Windows Key + R` — Open the Run dialog. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)
- `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` — Open Task Manager. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Aero must be active to view thumbnails. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/taskbar-extensions), T1)
- When there are more thumbnails than can be displayed, the preview reverts to the legacy thumbnail or a standard icon. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/taskbar-extensions), T1)
- The page says behavior can depend on the Windows 11 version. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- Recent Windows 11 builds, especially 24H2 and newer, may ignore older methods for fully disabling taskbar thumbnails. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- The page recommends trying supported Windows settings first, then using ExtendedUIHoverTime to delay previews if they still appear. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- The post describes the issue on Windows 11 Home on an HP OmniBook X Flip 16-ar0014ca Next Gen AI Laptop and reports reproduction on many Windows 11 laptops, including premium models. No build, channel, Copilot+ PC, region, or rollout limit is stated. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The accepted answer says there is no supported registry key to disable previews entirely and that the registry tweak is undocumented and not guaranteed to persist across feature updates. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5706626/windows-11-how-to-disable-the-preview-on-the-task?page=1), T5)
- The question author says they use a corporate laptop and do not have registry access. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5706626/windows-11-how-to-disable-the-preview-on-the-task?page=1), T5)
- After the PowerShell command, Explorer should restart automatically. If it does not, sign out and back in, or restart Windows. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- The user reports that restarting Windows Explorer did not resolve the issue. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)
- The user says Microsoft had commented on a Feedback Hub post that the glitch was fixed, but it still occurred for them. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)
- The final reply asks the user to wait for a new Microsoft update. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The accepted answer says Windows 10 had legacy registry flags that allowed hover previews to be suppressed, and that Microsoft removed those flags in Windows 11. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5706626/windows-11-how-to-disable-the-preview-on-the-task?page=1), T5)
- In Windows Vista, hovering over an application's taskbar button displays a thumbnail representing the running window. If the taskbar has collapsed the application's windows, the thumbnail appears as a stack, but only the active window is shown in the thumbnail itself. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/taskbar-extensions), T1)
- In Windows 7, each member of a group is shown as a separate thumbnail and is also a switch target. Applications can provide thumbnails and switch targets for child windows, documents, or tabs that would not normally appear in the taskbar. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/taskbar-extensions), T1)
- The page describes Enable Peek in Performance Options as an older Windows setting that may still help on some systems. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([github.com](https://github.com/handsomegary/disable-windows-peek-guide), T2)
- The user says the thumbnail preview disappeared instantly when minimizing this way on their previous Dell laptop running Windows 10. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- System Properties: Advanced > Settings under Performance. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)
- Settings → System → Storage → Temporary files → Thumbnails. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)
- Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects. ([h30434.www3.hp.com](https://h30434.www3.hp.com/t5/Notebook-Video-Display-and-Touch/Windows-11-taskbar-thumbnail-preview-slow-at-disappointing/td-p/9665760), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The behavior applies when the taskbar is set to uncombined, an app has multiple windows open, and there is not enough taskbar space. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/march-26-2026-kb5079489-os-build-28000-1764-preview-cd374a56-9657-43fb-9ebe-40cb693d8d10), T1)
- The update is delivered through gradual rollout, so availability varies by device, or normal rollout to all eligible devices. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/march-26-2026-kb5079489-os-build-28000-1764-preview-cd374a56-9657-43fb-9ebe-40cb693d8d10), T1)
- The page recommends Windows 11 22H2 or newer and says the feature is most consistently available in 22H2, 23H2, and 24H2. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- On very large or high-resolution displays, more open apps or windows may be needed to trigger overflow. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- With multiple monitors, overflow behavior can vary by taskbar configuration. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- No SKU, hardware eligibility, region, or Insider/rollout conditions are stated. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- The overflow state appears when space is constrained and the taskbar is full. ([zdnet.com](https://www.zdnet.com/article/windows-11-taskbar-gets-this-new-overflow-section-to-keep-your-apps-under-control/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If overflow does not appear, the page suggests opening more apps or windows; very large or high-resolution displays may require more windows. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- The exact overflow indicator and right-click options can vary by Windows 11 version and updates. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- For an older Windows 11 build with different options or behavior, the page suggests updating Windows. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 manages overflow differently: taskbar buttons can shrink and combine, and users use “Taskbar buttons” settings. The Windows 11 Taskbar overflow behavior described on the page is not the same as Windows 10. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/enable-and-use-windows-11s-taskbar-overflow-system-tray-settings-to-reduce-clutter.402551/?amp=1), T5)
- The page says the earlier mainstream Windows 11 release let users choose which apps to place in the overflow area; the reintroduced experience automatically creates a set of overflowed apps. ([zdnet.com](https://www.zdnet.com/article/windows-11-taskbar-gets-this-new-overflow-section-to-keep-your-apps-under-control/), T4)

- `WinKey + B` — Moves focus to the system tray and “Show Hidden Icons” button. ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)
- `Alt+Shift+Left/Right` — Reorders tray icons, according to a contributor. ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)
- `Win+I` — Opens Settings. ([allthings.how](https://allthings.how/how-to-hide-system-tray-overflow-menu-from-taskbar-on-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Quiet time is defined as the first hour after a new user logs into their account for the first time, or for the first time after an operating-system upgrade or clean installation. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- During quiet time, most notifications should not be sent or shown. Feedback expected in response to a user action, such as plugging in a USB device or printing a document, is an exception described by the page. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Notifications sent during quiet time are discarded unshown. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Notifications sent when the user is away are queued for display. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The system uses SHQueryUserNotificationState to check whether the user is in quiet time, away from the computer, or in an uninterruptable state such as Presentation mode. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The page states no SKU, hardware, region, Insider, or rollout conditions. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The icons present depend on which background processes or apps are running; the page notes that an icon may not appear unless its app is running. ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)
- The number of icons shown varies with what is running and which icons are configured for constant display. ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)
- The page says control of the System Tray Overflow Menu is available in Windows 11 version 22H2 or later. ([allthings.how](https://allthings.how/how-to-hide-system-tray-overflow-menu-from-taskbar-on-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Before installing a non-transient icon in the notification area, the user should be asked for permission and given the option, normally through its shortcut menu, to remove the icon. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Users can suppress all notifications from an application on Windows 7. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Notifications should be ignorable and should not require immediate user action; none is so important that it should override quiet time. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- If an application uses a custom notification method that does not use Shell_NotifyIcon, IUserNotification, or IUserNotification2, it should explicitly call SHQueryUserNotificationState to determine whether to display notification UI. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The page recommends high-DPI-aware icons, providing 16x16 and 32x32 pixel icons and using LoadIconMetric. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section describes taskbar icon controls under Notification area: Select which icons appear on the taskbar and Turn system icons on or off. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- On Windows 7, newly added notification-area icons go to the overflow section by default. Only the user can promote an icon from the overflow to the notification area, although the system can temporarily promote one as a short preview in certain circumstances. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Windows 7 allows a user to suppress all notifications from an application and introduces quiet time. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- A GUID registered for the icon is the preferred identification method on Windows 7 and later. On Windows Vista and earlier, the icon is identified by the handle of an associated window plus an application-defined icon identifier. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The notification timeout setting is ignored in Windows Vista and later in favor of a system-wide accessibility timeout setting. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The page does not describe Windows 11-specific differences. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- The page states that Windows 10 and Windows 11 let users choose which system tray icons stay on constant display and which reside in the hidden icons/overflow area. ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Options opens the Notification Area Icons item in Control Panel. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area), T1)
- Taskbar settings ([nvda.groups.io](https://nvda.groups.io/g/chat/topic/windows_11_navigating_the/104079234), T5)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Other system tray icons ([allthings.how](https://allthings.how/how-to-hide-system-tray-overflow-menu-from-taskbar-on-windows-11/), T4)
- Taskbar context menu > Taskbar settings > Other system tray icons ([allthings.how](https://allthings.how/how-to-hide-system-tray-overflow-menu-from-taskbar-on-windows-11/), T4)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Shell_NotifyIcon` | Adds, modifies, or deletes an icon in the notification area; can also display a notification. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NOTIFYICONDATA` | Structure sent to Shell_NotifyIcon containing information for the notification-area icon and notification. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4` | Recommended notification-area icon version, introduced in Windows Vista; provides full available functionality, including identification through a registered GUID, a superior callback mechanism, and better accessibility. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NIM_ADD, NIM_MODIFY, NIM_DELETE, NIM_SETVERSION` | Shell_NotifyIcon operation values used in the page's examples to add, modify, delete, or set the icon version. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NIF_ICON, NIF_TIP, NIF_GUID, NIF_INFO` | NOTIFYICONDATA flags shown or discussed for specifying icon information, tooltip information, GUID identification, or notification information. The page says not to set NIF_INFO when adding an icon without displaying a n | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NIIF_RESPECT_QUIET_TIME` | NOTIFYICONDATA flag for whether the notification should respect quiet time. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `Shell_NotifyIconGetRect` | Retrieves the notification-area icon's bounding rectangle. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `LoadIconMetric` | Loads and scales the correct icon appropriately for high-DPI notification-area icons. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `CalculatePopupWindowPosition` | Determines the location for a popup window or dialog box shown in response to a notification-area icon click. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `SHQueryUserNotificationState` | Checks whether the user is in quiet time, away from the computer, or in an uninterruptable state such as Presentation mode. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `IUserNotification and IUserNotification2` | COM wrappers for Shell_NotifyIcon; the page says they do not provide the full NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4 functionality available through Shell_NotifyIcon directly, including use of a GUID to identify the notification-area icon | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |
| `NIF_GUID` | NOTIFYICONDATA flag used in the example to identify the notification-area icon through a GUID. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/notification-area) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win + I` — Open Settings, then navigate to Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors. ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- BadgeNotificationManager requires package identity. If the app doesn't have package identity, for example because it's unpackaged, calls to SetBadgeAsCount, SetBadgeAsGlyph, and ClearBadge throw an exception. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges), T1)
- Badges can be displayed whether or not the app is running; a taskbar badge appears when the app is pinned to the taskbar even if the app isn't running. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges), T1)
- Badges appear only when an app supplies a supported taskbar badge; Windows does not invent one. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- Focus sessions can temporarily turn off taskbar badges and flashing. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- Widgets notification behavior is controlled separately through Widgets settings. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- For an app without package identity, BadgeNotificationManager calls to SetBadgeAsCount, SetBadgeAsGlyph, and ClearBadge throw an exception. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges), T1)
- Changing Show badges on taskbar apps applies immediately; no sign-out, restart, Registry edit, Group Policy change, or app reinstall is required. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- The badge option does not control desktop notification banners, sounds, Notification Center entries, in-app counters, Start menu badges, browser-tab indicators, or taskbar-button flashing. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- The page states that there is no standard per-app badge toggle in Taskbar behaviors. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- The page says an app's pending attention request can keep the taskbar visible on purpose. ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)
- The page describes installers and updaters with progress bars as possible sources of flashing taskbar buttons. ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- For Windows App SDK 1.7 or later, the page recommends BadgeNotificationManager instead of the UWP BadgeUpdateManager API. The UWP API builds an XML payload. No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges), T1)
- The page describes the Show flashing on taskbar apps and Show badges on taskbar apps controls under Windows 11 taskbar behaviors; it does not state that Windows 10 has these controls. ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- Settings > System > Focus ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- Settings > System > Notifications ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/windows-11-show-or-hide-taskbar-app-notification-badges.443587/), T5)
- Taskbar settings > Taskbar behaviors > Show flashing on taskbar apps ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)
- Taskbar settings > Taskbar behaviors > Show badges on taskbar apps ([w3tutorials.net](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/fix-taskbar-wont-hide/), T4)

| `Microsoft.Windows.BadgeNotifications namespace` | Namespace containing BadgeNotificationManager. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges) |

| `BadgeNotificationManager.Current` | Gets the BadgeNotificationManager instance for the app. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges) |
| `SetBadgeAsCount` | Sets a numeric badge; values greater than 99 display as “99+”. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/badges) |

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The feature supports agents across first- and third-party apps; Researcher in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app is the first adopter. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/04/april-30-2026-kb5083631-os-builds-26200-8328-and-26100-8328-preview), T1)
