- The update has gradual and normal rollout phases, so availability can vary by device. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/04/april-30-2026-kb5083631-os-builds-26200-8328-and-26100-8328-preview), T1)
- The page does not state SKU, hardware, or region requirements. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/04/april-30-2026-kb5083631-os-builds-26200-8328-and-26100-8328-preview), T1)
- The page does not mention “Ask Copilot on the taskbar.” ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/04/april-30-2026-kb5083631-os-builds-26200-8328-and-26100-8328-preview), T1)
- Listed under “Gradual rollout”; availability may vary by device. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/04/17/releasing-windows-11-builds-26100-8313-and-26200-8313-to-the-release-preview-channel/), T1)
- Supports agents across first- and third-party apps; Researcher in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app is the first adopter. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/04/17/releasing-windows-11-builds-26100-8313-and-26200-8313-to-the-release-preview-channel/), T1)
- The described progress and notification occur while Researcher works on a report and when the report is ready. ([Windows Insider Blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/04/17/releasing-windows-11-builds-26100-8313-and-26200-8313-to-the-release-preview-channel/), T1)
- The page says AI agents are being integrated into the Windows 11 taskbar and that Microsoft has confirmed the capability. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/19/sorry-microsoft-windows-10-taskbar-is-still-better-than-windows-11-and-heres-why/), T4)
- The page says Ask Copilot is coming to the Windows 11 taskbar in mid-2026. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/19/sorry-microsoft-windows-10-taskbar-is-still-better-than-windows-11-and-heres-why/), T4)
- The page does not state any SKU, hardware, regional, or Insider-rollout requirements. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/19/sorry-microsoft-windows-10-taskbar-is-still-better-than-windows-11-and-heres-why/), T4)
- The taskbar agent feature is described as optional and not turned on automatically. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/18/microsoft-confirms-ai-agents-are-still-coming-to-the-windows-11-taskbar-as-it-prepares-for-public-rollout/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 has no equivalent of the taskbar AI-agent feature and no concept of AI orchestration, according to the page. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/19/sorry-microsoft-windows-10-taskbar-is-still-better-than-windows-11-and-heres-why/), T4)
- Windows 10 search sent users to Edge with a Bing result; the page contrasts this with Ask Copilot, which can replace Search. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/06/19/sorry-microsoft-windows-10-taskbar-is-still-better-than-windows-11-and-heres-why/), T4)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Windows.UI.Shell.Tasks API` | Developers can learn how to use this API for the Agents on Taskbar experience. | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2026/04/april-30-2026-kb5083631-os-builds-26200-8328-and-26100-8328-preview) |
| `Windows Agent API` | The article says third-party developers may integrate their agents into their apps using this API. | [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/18/microsoft-confirms-ai-agents-are-still-coming-to-the-windows-11-taskbar-as-it-prepares-for-public-rollout/) |
| `Model Context Protocol (MCP)` | Described as powering the agent experience and allowing AI models or agents to connect to apps or files, including the operating system. | [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/18/microsoft-confirms-ai-agents-are-still-coming-to-the-windows-11-taskbar-as-it-prepares-for-public-rollout/) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + S` — Open the search box. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- `Win+I` — Open Settings. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- `Win+S` — Use Windows Search. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The current-user Search box and Search icon and label REG options are stated to be available starting with Windows 11 build 25252. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- The all-users Group Policy and REG options are stated to be available starting with Windows 11 build 25295. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- The Local Group Policy Editor option requires administrator sign-in and is available only in Windows 11 Pro, Enterprise, and Education. The page says all editions can use the all-users REG option instead. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- The Search box height increase by 4 pixels is stated for Windows 11 build 26300.8772 (Experimental 26H2) for Insiders. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The REG-file instructions say to approve the merge through Run, Yes (UAC), Yes, and OK. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- When the all-users policy is specified, current-user Settings and REG options are overridden and grayed out. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section describes a different entry point: right-click the taskbar and select Search. Its stated options are Hidden, Show search icon only, Show search box, Show search highlights, and Open on hover. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Search for anything, anywhere. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/add-or-remove-search-button-on-taskbar-in-windows-11.1197/), T5)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Search ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4mBPgKnJ0KY), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Enhanced mode affects battery life and performance. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-use-search-correctly-on-windows-11), T4)
- The page says the device must be plugged into a power source for Enhanced mode's initial index. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-use-search-correctly-on-windows-11), T4)
- The page states no SKU, hardware, region, or Insider/rollout requirements. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-use-search-correctly-on-windows-11), T4)
- The page recommends treating Enhanced indexing as a targeted convenience setting, not a blanket recommendation. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-search-enable-enhanced-indexing-without-bing-registry-risks.438677/), T5)
- Folders can be excluded to control the index scope; indexing large source trees, VM folders, game libraries, backup archives, or development caches can increase disk activity and database size. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-search-enable-enhanced-indexing-without-bing-registry-risks.438677/), T5)
- The initial crawl should be allowed to finish before judging results; an index rebuild can take up to 24 hours in some cases. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-search-enable-enhanced-indexing-without-bing-registry-risks.438677/), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + W` — Open the Widgets board. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- `Win + W` — Opens the Widgets board. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The swipe-from-the-side gesture is specified for when the taskbar is aligned to the center. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- In the current release, only packaged apps can be registered as widget providers. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs), T1)
- In the current release, the only supported widget host is the Widgets Board. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs), T1)
- Widget customization is supported starting with Windows App SDK 1.4; the article says to update the NuGet package reference to the latest version. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs), T1)
- The sample requires developer mode to be enabled. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs), T1)
- The new defaults are described as under testing and gradually rolling out to Windows Insiders in Windows 11 Insider Experimental Preview Build 26300.8346. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- The article does not state SKU, hardware, or region requirements. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- The article does not give a date for availability to regular users. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- The Feed control was rolled out incrementally and may be absent in older builds or some Insider flights. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Enterprise policies or device management may block or reconfigure Widgets controls. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Some widgets may require a Microsoft account sign-in or permissions such as location access. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- The page does not specify a Windows SKU, hardware requirement, or region. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The article reports a known bug with the Windows Widget Board for widgets built using the Windows App SDK: the ellipsis menu can become unresponsive after the customization card is shown. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs), T1)
- The article says to click “Turn off” when prompted after turning off “Feed”. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- If Show or hide feeds is missing, the build may not include the option; the page suggests checking for OS updates and considering whether the device is managed. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- If the hover setting is missing or does not stick, the page advises trying the built-in toggle first; it mentions restarting explorer.exe if the setting fails to stick. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- The page says some builds may re-enable taskbar notifications after feature updates, so the settings may need to be checked again. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Unexpected widget placement after rearranging may be related to a current flight issue or OS version; the page suggests checking known issues or updating. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 taskbar layout section describes News and interests and its Show news and interests on the taskbar switch; it does not describe the Windows 11 Widgets board controls. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Taskbar settings > Taskbar items > Widgets ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- Widgets > settings icon > Open Widgets board on hover ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- Widgets > settings icon > Show or hide feeds > Feed ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Widgets ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/05/03/microsoft-is-finally-turning-off-the-msn-feed-and-ads-in-windows-11-widgets-by-default/), T4)
- Widgets board → Settings (cog) → Show or hide feeds / Feed ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Widgets board → Settings (cog) → Open Widgets board on hover ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Widgets board → Settings (cog) → Notifications ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)
- Settings → Privacy & security ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/turn-windows-11-widgets-into-a-productive-dashboard-in-five-steps.404939/), T5)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `IWidgetProvider` | Interface whose methods the widget host invokes to request widget data or let the provider respond to user actions. The article implements CreateWidget, DeleteWidget, OnActionInvoked, OnWidgetContextChanged, Activate, an | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `IWidgetProvider2` | Interface that exposes widget customization through the OnCustomizationRequested callback. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `IWidgetProviderAnalytics` | The article says OnAnalyticsInfoReported is raised when the user closes customization without the app-defined exit action. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetAnalyticsInfoReportedArgs.AnalyticsJson` | The article says its interactionKind is "exitCustomization" when the user closes customization without clicking the app-defined exit action. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetContext` | Provides widget context used by provider callbacks, including the widget ID, definition ID, and size. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetActionInvokedArgs` | Provides the action Verb, WidgetContext, and Data to OnActionInvoked. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetCustomizationRequestedArgs` | Provides the WidgetContext to OnCustomizationRequested. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetContextChangedArgs` | Provides the WidgetContext when the widget context changes; the article says this currently occurs when the user changes a pinned widget's size. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetManager.GetDefault` | Gets the default WidgetManager instance. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetManager.GetWidgetInfos` | Returns WidgetInfo objects for widgets the provider is currently serving, allowing the provider to restore widget IDs, names, and custom state at startup. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetUpdateRequestOptions` | Carries the widget ID, Template, Data, and CustomState for an update. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `WidgetManager.UpdateWidget` | Sends updated widget data to the widget host. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `Action.Execute` | Adaptive Cards action type used by the sample widget for the "inc", "reset", and "exitCustomization" verbs. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `CoRegisterClassObject` | Registers the widget provider class object with OLE so the widget host can communicate with the provider; the sample passes flags 0x4 and 0x1. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |
| `CoRevokeClassObject` | Revokes the registered class object when the sample provider exits. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Windows/apps/develop/widgets/implement-widget-provider-cs) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + A` — Open Quick Settings. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- `Windows + A` — Open Quick Settings. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- `Windows + Ctrl + V` — Open the sound output page. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- `Windows + Ctrl + L` — Turn on Live captions. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- `Windows + K` — Open the wireless-display casting list. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- `Windows + N` — Open notifications and the calendar, not Quick Settings. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- `Win + A` — Opens Quick Settings, as stated in the page introduction. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHlpHHGdE6M), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page says the battery icon represents battery status on laptops and tablets. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- The battery icon is described as representing battery status on laptops and tablets. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/help/29280), T1)
- Tile availability depends on the PC's hardware: Bluetooth needs a Bluetooth adapter and driver; the battery indicator and battery controls require a battery; the brightness slider requires a built-in screen; hearing device presets require Bluetooth LE Audio hearing aids and a compatible PC. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Bluetooth may be missing if Windows cannot detect the adapter, its driver is missing, or Airplane mode is on. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- The page says a managed work or school PC may have layout policies enforced centrally; gpedit.msc troubleshooting steps are given for a personal Windows 11 Pro PC. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Quick Settings is disabled by design for a kiosk (assigned access) user, according to the page. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- No Copilot+ PC, region, or Insider-rollout requirement is stated. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page recommends reopening Quick Settings and checking that moved tiles are in their new positions, then checking again after a restart. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- For missing Bluetooth or Wi-Fi tiles, the page suggests checking Airplane mode, scrolling all pages, inspecting Device Manager, updating drivers, checking Windows Update and restarting. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- If Device Manager shows no adapter, the page says the PC has no such hardware and the tile cannot appear. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- The page says changes may be blocked by the Disable editing quick settings policy, and that the Remove Quick Settings policy needs a restart. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- In Windows 11 22H2 and 23H2, Quick Settings uses a fixed set of pinned buttons; users edit the list to pin or unpin buttons. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- In Windows 11 24H2 and later, the panel is scrollable, all supported quick actions are already in the list, and users rearrange tiles rather than adding or removing them. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Before 24H2 the battery tile is called Battery saver; in 24H2 and later it is called Energy saver. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Before 24H2, Live captions is inside the Accessibility flyout; from 24H2 it also has its own tile. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > About ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Settings > Windows Update ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Start Menu and Taskbar > Disable editing quick settings ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Start Menu and Taskbar > Simplify Quick Settings Layout ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)
- User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Start Menu and Taskbar > Remove Quick Settings ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-customize-the-quick-settings-panel-in-windows-11-24h2.html), T4)

- The page does not describe a Wi-Fi sub-panel or Bluetooth sub-panel; it describes the Bluetooth tile and Quick Settings navigation. ([technobezz.com](https://www.technobezz.com/how-to-open-and-use-bluetooth-and-devices-settings-in-windows), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions say to select the Network icon and Up arrow, then choose a Wi-Fi network and select Connect. - The Windows 10 instructions also say to choose Yes or No based on the network type and whether the PC should be discoverable by other PCs and devices. The page states no corresponding Windows 11 step. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/connect-to-a-wi-fi-network-in-windows), T1)
- The page says older Windows 10 guides may refer to the Action Center Bluetooth tile. ([technobezz.com](https://www.technobezz.com/how-to-open-and-use-bluetooth-and-devices-settings-in-windows), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `WIN + CTRL + V` — Open the volume mixer quickly. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/servicing/os/windows-11/2023/10/october-31-2023-kb5031455-os-builds-22621-2506-and-22631-2506-preview), T1)
- `Windows + A` — Opens Quick Settings. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Space` — Activates a focused control, as described by the page. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Enter` — Activates a focused control, as described by the page. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` — Opens Task Manager. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Windows key + A` — Opens or closes Quick Settings. ([techlasi.com](https://techlasi.com/savvy/how-to-open-action-center-in-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page states that Windows 11 displays controls when a supported app, website, or browser tab is actively playing or has recently played media. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The app or website must share media session information with Windows; available controls and metadata vary by source. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- For browser media, a tab may fail to provide controls if it is closed, suspended, muted, or prevented from starting playback. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page states no SKU, Copilot+ PC, region, or Insider/rollout requirements. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Media controls appear above the toggles only while audio or video is actively playing. ([techlasi.com](https://techlasi.com/savvy/how-to-open-action-center-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page does not state any hardware, SKU, region, Insider, or rollout requirements for media controls. ([techlasi.com](https://techlasi.com/savvy/how-to-open-action-center-in-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If the card is missing, start playback in the source app or tab and reopen Quick Settings. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Unsupported players or sites may show limited information, omit controls, or provide no media card. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The page recommends restarting the app or browser, updating apps and Windows, checking the output device, or restarting Windows Explorer if controls are frozen or unresponsive. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Volume controls do not pause media, and playback controls do not adjust system volume. ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 combined notifications and quick toggles in one Action Center panel; Windows 11 split them into Quick Settings and Notification Center. ([techlasi.com](https://techlasi.com/savvy/how-to-open-action-center-in-windows-11/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Sound ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Audio ([freedom251.com](https://freedom251.com/how-to-use-the-universal-media-controls-in-windows-11/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + N` — Opens the calendar and notification center flyout. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page says the feature is being enabled server-side in a phased rollout for subsets of users. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-calendar-flyout-returns-as-ignite-2025-highlights-agentic-copilot.390179/), T5)
- The feature is associated with October preview/Release Preview updates, including KB5067036 for Windows 11 24H2/25H2. The update details identify KB5067036 as an optional preview update released October 28, 2025, and list the General Availability Channel. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-calendar-flyout-returns-as-ignite-2025-highlights-agentic-copilot.390179/), T5)
- No Copilot+ hardware requirement or region requirement is stated specifically for the calendar flyout. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-calendar-flyout-returns-as-ignite-2025-highlights-agentic-copilot.390179/), T5)
- The article describes the Windows 11 Agenda view as an upcoming change, without specifying a build, channel, SKU, hardware requirement, or region. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/11/20/windows-11-is-getting-windows-10-like-calendar-agenda-in-notification-center-with-outlook-and-sadly-ai-features/), T4)
- Microsoft 365 Copilot integration is stated to begin rolling out in December 2025. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/11/20/windows-11-is-getting-windows-10-like-calendar-agenda-in-notification-center-with-outlook-and-sadly-ai-features/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section refers to the notification area and Action center; it describes editing quick actions through Notifications & Actions and Edit your quick actions. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/personalization/customize-the-taskbar-in-windows), T1)
- Windows 10 provided a chronological agenda, scheduled meetings, and quick access to create events from the date/time area; Windows 11 removed much of that functionality in 2021. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-calendar-flyout-returns-as-ignite-2025-highlights-agentic-copilot.390179/), T5)
- The page says Windows 11 replaced the Windows 10 functionality with a visually simplified clock and a less useful notification center. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-calendar-flyout-returns-as-ignite-2025-highlights-agentic-copilot.390179/), T5)
- On Windows 10, clicking the taskbar clock opens a small calendar flyout with an Agenda list; users can hide agendas and open events in Calendar / Outlook apps. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/11/20/windows-11-is-getting-windows-10-like-calendar-agenda-in-notification-center-with-outlook-and-sadly-ai-features/), T4)
- The Windows 11 Agenda view is described as bringing back the Windows 10 idea in a modern form. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/11/20/windows-11-is-getting-windows-10-like-calendar-agenda-in-notification-center-with-outlook-and-sadly-ai-features/), T4)
- The Notification Center clock is described as matching the one in Windows 10, with an option to turn seconds off. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/11/20/windows-11-is-getting-windows-10-like-calendar-agenda-in-notification-center-with-outlook-and-sadly-ai-features/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + N` — Open the Windows 11 notification center. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/notifications-and-do-not-disturb-in-windows-feeca47f-0baf-5680-16f0-8801db1a8466?device=c), T1)
- `Windows key + A` — Open the Windows 10 notification center/action center. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/notifications-and-do-not-disturb-in-windows-feeca47f-0baf-5680-16f0-8801db1a8466?device=c), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Urgent/important notifications require Windows Insider Preview Build 22546 or later, as stated by the page. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- Reminder and alarm scenarios require at least one button; otherwise the notification is treated as a normal notification. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- Additional context menu actions count toward the maximum of 5 buttons. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- The page does not state a general banner timeout or standard notification expiration rule. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page does not state a banner timeout duration or describe what happens when a banner times out. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/notifications-and-do-not-disturb-in-windows-feeca47f-0baf-5680-16f0-8801db1a8466?device=c), T1)
- Not stated. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- The page says event handlers for activated, dismissed, and failed events are not supported. ([libraries.io](https://libraries.io/nimble/win11toast), T4)
- The page says true progress updates require additional WinRT interfaces; the implementation shows static progress bars. ([libraries.io](https://libraries.io/nimble/win11toast), T4)
- The page says COM server registration is required for activation when the app is closed and is outside the library's scope. ([libraries.io](https://libraries.io/nimble/win11toast), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 11 uses the term notification center and the shortcut Windows key + N; Windows 10 uses action center in its notification instructions and the shortcut Windows key + A. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/notifications-and-do-not-disturb-in-windows-feeca47f-0baf-5680-16f0-8801db1a8466?device=c), T1)
- Windows 10 instructions describe clearing all notifications with Clear all notifications and app notifications with the settings button; Windows 11 instructions use Clear all and the more button. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/notifications-and-do-not-disturb-in-windows-feeca47f-0baf-5680-16f0-8801db1a8466?device=c), T1)
- The page says “toast notification” and “app notification” refer to the same Windows feature; “toast notification” is being phased out in documentation. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- On older devices, added context menu actions appear as normal buttons. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- For attribution text on older Windows versions that do not support it, the text is displayed as another text element, if the three-text-element maximum has not already been reached. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- On Windows Mobile, reminders show pre-expanded; incoming call notifications display full screen. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- For Windows App SDK apps, button activation always launches the app in the foreground; background activation is explicitly supported for UWP apps. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- The attribution area’s ellipses menu lets the user go to the Windows Settings page for the app’s notifications or quickly disable notifications for the app. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)
- Important-notification behavior can be modified in notification settings. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/adaptive-interactive-toasts), T1)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows + N` — Opens the notification center and calendar. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- `Windows + I` — Opens Settings. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- `Windows + A` — Opens Quick Settings; the page states that the Do not disturb toggle is not there by default. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win + R` — Opens Run, where entering ms-settings:notifications and pressing Enter opens the Notifications settings page. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page states Windows 11 Home does not include gpedit.msc; it identifies Group Policy Editor availability for Pro, Enterprise, and Education. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Focus sessions require the Clock app; if it has been uninstalled, the page says to reinstall it from the Microsoft Store. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page lists schedules, display duplication, gaming, full-screen apps, and the first hour after a Windows feature update as automatic Do not disturb triggers. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Starting a focus session turns Do not disturb on for the session's duration by default. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says that if Do not disturb was enabled before a focus session began, ending the session leaves it enabled. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says the notification-center toggle is on Windows + N, not in Quick Settings opened with Windows + A. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page states that an administrator may enforce the older Quiet Hours policy on a managed computer; the user may not be able to change the setting and may need to contact the organization’s administrator. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says a work or school policy may control Do not disturb. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Settings pages can vary by Windows version and edition. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- No SKU, hardware, Copilot+ PC, region, or Insider/rollout restriction is stated. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page says the taskbar clock area shows a Do not disturb indicator, described as a bell with a sleep symbol. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says alerts received while Do not disturb is on remain in the notification center. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page recommends checking the automatic rules if Do not disturb turns on again. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says a focus session ending does not necessarily turn Do not disturb off. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page states that most notification banners and sounds are suppressed while Do not disturb is enabled, but muted notifications remain available in Notification Center and are not normally deleted or lost. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- Priority apps, alarms, and reminders may still be allowed. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- A Focus session normally turns on Do not disturb, hides taskbar badges and flashing, and shows a timer; a notification appears when the session ends. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- If Do not disturb was already enabled before a Focus session, it remains enabled after the session ends. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- Changing Focus settings alone will not disable manually enabled or scheduled Do not disturb. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- Do not confuse the global Notifications switch with Do not disturb: turning global notifications off disables Windows notifications generally and does not configure Do not disturb schedules, priority apps, or Focus behavior. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- If Do not disturb turns on again, the page recommends checking automatic rules, active Focus sessions, and work or school policy. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section describes Focus assist (also called quiet hours in earlier versions of Windows 10), with Priority only, Alarms only, or Off modes. It also describes automatic rules such as During these times. The Windows 11 section uses Do not disturb and Focus sessions. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- Windows 8.1 called the feature Quiet Hours and placed it in Action Center / settings. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Windows 10 called it Focus assist and placed it at Settings > System > Focus assist. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Windows 11 22H2 and later calls it Do not disturb and places it at Settings > System > Notifications. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Windows 10's Action Center layout put the toggle in the Quick Settings/Action Center flyout, unlike current Windows 11. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says the older Settings > System > Focus assist path applies mainly to Windows 10 and legacy Windows documentation; current Windows 11 primarily presents the former Focus Assist controls as Do not disturb under Settings > System > Notifications. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- Windows still documents the older Focus Assist or Quiet Hours URI, ms-settings:quiethours; the page says it may work on some systems but recommends ms-settings:notifications for current Windows 11 controls. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- The page mentions Quiet Hours as an older policy-backed feature name. No Windows 7 difference is stated. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > System > Notifications ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- Start > Settings > System > Focus ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- Settings > System > Notifications ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Focus ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Notifications > Set priority notifications ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Info > Create report ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/turn-off-focus-assist-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Notifications > Turn on do not disturb automatically ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- ms-settings:notifications ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)
- ms-settings:quiethours (legacy URI; may work on some systems, but the page recommends ms-settings:notifications for current Windows 11 controls) ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-disable-or-enable-configure-focus-assist-on-windows-11/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key Tab` — Open Task view. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/4028538/configure-multiple-desktops-in-windows), T1)
- `Windows logo key` — Runs “Task View”. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044672/), T4)
- `Enter key` — Applies the typed name when renaming a desktop. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044672/), T4)
- `Win + Tab` — Open the Desktops view. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)
- `Win + Ctrl + D` — Create a new desktop. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)
- `Win + Ctrl + Left/Right Arrow` — Cycle between desktops. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)
- `Alt + Shift Left/Right Arrow` — Move desktops. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Applicable products stated: Notebook, Desktop, All-in-One PC, Gaming Handheld, MiniPC. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044672/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions say to create a desktop using [New desktop] in Task View and to move open windows between desktops by dragging them. They do not describe renaming, reordering, or closing desktops. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044672/), T4)
- The feature was introduced in Windows 10 with the built-in Task View button on the taskbar. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)
- Windows 11 removed the Windows timeline that showed recent activity and replaced it with the Desktops icon. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/135079/how-to-manage-virtual-desktops-in-windows-11), T4)

- `Windows key + I` — Open Settings. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- `Windows key + Ctrl + Right Arrow` — Switch to the next virtual desktop. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- A different background picture can be selected for each desktop. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- Configuring a background picture per monitor isn't supported when using multiple desktops. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- Slideshow as a background isn't supported when using multiple desktops. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- At least two virtual desktops are needed to assign different wallpapers across desktops. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Use Picture mode; the page states per-virtual-desktop backgrounds are supported for still pictures, not slideshow or a different solid color per desktop. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Keep the image files available. Moving, deleting, renaming, or disconnecting the source can cause a wallpaper to revert or appear black. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Windows does not support assigning distinct wallpapers by both virtual desktop and physical monitor at the same time. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- A theme change can replace configured wallpapers. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Administrator rights, a Microsoft account, a restart, and Registry changes are not required. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- On a managed work or school PC, organization policy may enforce a wallpaper; the page advises not to edit the Registry or bypass policy and to contact the organization’s IT administrator. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Use Picture mode; the page states that per-virtual-desktop custom backgrounds support still pictures, not Slideshow, Solid color, or Windows spotlight. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- At least two virtual desktops are needed to assign wallpapers to multiple desktops; at least two image files are needed for visibly different wallpapers. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- To verify, switch desktops and confirm the wallpaper changes, switch back and confirm the original returns, then open Task View and verify the desktops remain listed. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- If all desktops show the same wallpaper, assign the image to a specific desktop rather than choosing Set for all desktops. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- If a wallpaper is black, missing, or changes after reconnecting a drive, check whether its source file moved, was deleted or renamed, or is unavailable; store it in a stable local folder and reassign it. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- If a specific-desktop choice is unavailable, confirm multiple virtual desktops exist and Personalize your background is set to Picture; otherwise use Choose background from the target desktop’s Task View thumbnail. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- If an organization-managed wallpaper reverts or settings are unavailable, check Settings > Accounts > Access work or school and contact the organization’s IT administrator. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Verify by switching desktops and confirming the wallpaper changes, then switching back and confirming the original returns; Task View should still show the desktops. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- If every desktop gets the same wallpaper, assign the image to the target desktop rather than choosing Set for all desktops. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- If the wallpaper changes back, use Picture mode and reselect the image on each desktop. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- If the wallpaper is black or missing, check whether the source file was moved, deleted, renamed, or made unavailable; store images in a stable local folder and reassign them. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- If an individual-desktop choice is unavailable, confirm multiple desktops exist and Picture mode is selected; alternatively use Task View > right-click desktop > Choose background. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- If a work or school PC enforces wallpaper settings, the page advises contacting the organization’s IT administrator rather than bypassing policy. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page says Windows 10 uses the same core Task View workflow, though the taskbar appearance and Settings layout may differ. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- The page states Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025. It does not describe Windows 7. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Windows 10 uses the same core Task View workflow, but its taskbar appearance and Settings layout may differ from Windows 11. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)
- The page states that Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-tutorials.305/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/?amp=1), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Personalization > Background ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/change-the-desktop-background-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Personalization > Themes ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)
- Settings > Accounts > Access work or school ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-different-wallpapers-for-each-virtual-desktop-in-windows-11.441497/), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Alt+Tab` — Display open windows; the Multitasking settings control app tabs and desktop scope for this view. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks-0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- `Alt + Tab` — See the current list of applications. ([support.lenovo.com](https://support.lenovo.com/us/en/solutions/ht515781), T4)
- `Tab while still holding Alt` — Cycle through the list of open applications. ([support.lenovo.com](https://support.lenovo.com/us/en/solutions/ht515781), T4)
- `Win+I` — Open Settings. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win+Ctrl+D` — Create and switch to a new virtual desktop. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win+Ctrl+← arrow` — Move to the previous virtual desktop. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win+Ctrl+F4` — Remove the current virtual desktop; its open windows move to the previous desktop. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win+Tab` — Open Task View, which is separate from Alt+Tab; the article says the Multitasking settings above do not apply to it in the same way. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The article says the options are available in Windows 11 Home and Pro; no administrator rights are needed to change them. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- The exact Edge-tab drop-down options may differ between Windows 11 builds. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Only Microsoft Edge gets separate tab entries in Alt+Tab; other browsers appear as a single window. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Edge must be running with more than one tab open for separate tab entries to appear. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A work- or school-managed PC may have options locked by an administrator. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Changes take effect immediately; no restart is needed. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If the Multitasking options are missing or different, the article recommends checking the Windows version with winver and installing pending Windows updates. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- If the Edge tabs do not appear, check that Edge has multiple tabs open and that the setting is not “Open windows only”; the article also suggests closing and reopening Edge. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section calls the desktop settings group Virtual desktops and uses the choice All desktops; the Windows 11 section calls the group Desktops and uses On all desktops. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks-0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- The Windows 10 section mentions a Timeline toggle. The Windows 11 section does not mention Timeline. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks-0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings › System › Multitasking ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings › Windows Update ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/customize-alttab-settings-in-windows-11/), T4)

| WA.08.04.i06 | Right-click an activity card and select Clear all from [date range]. | Clears activities from the selected date range. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/) |
| WA.08.04.i07 | Click the Task View button on the taskbar | Accesses Task View; Windows 10 version 1803 includes Timeline. | T4 | [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Desktop) |
| WA.08.04.i08 | Press Windows Key+Tab | Accesses Task View; Windows 10 version 1803 includes Timeline. | T4 | [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Desktop) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win+Tab` — Opens Timeline via Task View in Windows 10. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- `Windows Key+Tab` — Accesses Task View. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Desktop), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Timeline activity history was stored locally by default; cloud syncing was optional. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- Cross-device syncing used Microsoft accounts or enterprise Entra accounts. The article says cloud syncing was later discontinued for certain account types, without specifying dates or account details. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- Apps needed to register activities with the Graph API for Timeline support; the article says developer adoption was patchy. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Timeline remains on Windows 10, but its user experience was retired in Windows 11. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/ai-features/get-help-with-timeline), T1)
- The page recommends recent files, OneDrive, or app-based history for Windows 11 users; it also says web history can be accessed through a browser and recent files through OneDrive and Office. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/ai-features/get-help-with-timeline), T1)
- Windows 10 Timeline appeared in Task View and provided a time-based activity history. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- Windows 11 removed the Timeline user experience from Task View and replaced it with a simpler recent-items/recommended experience in the Start menu. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- The article says the Windows 11 replacement lacks Timeline’s time-based visualization and actionable activity cards. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- The article says the local Timeline experience remained on Windows 10 after cross-device syncing was limited or discontinued for some account types. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)
- Windows 10 version 1803 includes Timeline, which lets users view and open previously used apps over a certain period of time. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Desktop), T4)
- Timeline was removed in Windows 11. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Desktop), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Privacy > Activity history ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/), T5)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Graph API` | Apps had to register activities with it to support Timeline. | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/timeline-vs-recall-windows-history-features-and-privacy-tradeoffs.402181/) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + Z` — View the available grid layout options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- `Win + Z` — Invokes the menu that shows the available layouts. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- `Windows key + Z` — Opens the Snap Layouts menu. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The maximize caption button must be available for the system to automatically show snap layouts on hover. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- Customized caption buttons or a custom title bar may prevent the menu from appearing if the system cannot recognize the maximize button. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- The app's minimum window size may be too large for the window to fit in the selected zone. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- Support a minimum width of at most 500 effective pixels (epx) for snap layouts across the most common screen sizes; the page recommends 330 epx or less for compatibility with a larger set of devices and snap layouts. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- Layouts are tailored to screen size and orientation; the page gives large landscape screens and portrait screens as examples. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-snap-layout-menu), T1)
- The expanded selection of layouts, including options for positioning three windows side by side, is available only on wide displays with an effective resolution of at least 1850 pixels in width. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- Effective resolution is calculated by dividing the display’s native resolution by its scaling factor. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- The touchscreen drag-to-show-layouts variation was first available in Windows 11 version 22H2. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section describes snapping by dragging a window to the left or right edge of the screen; the Windows 11 section describes opening layout options by hovering over the maximize button or pressing Windows logo key + Z. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- The page says Windows 7 offered snapping two windows side by side, and Windows 10 supported up to four snaps. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- For Windows 11, the page describes Snap Layouts as adding visual guidance for snapping windows. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > System > Multitasking ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/make-it-easier-to-focus-on-tasks), T1)
- Settings > System > Multitasking > Snap windows ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- Settings > System > Multitasking ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Alt + Tab` — Displays Snap groups in the Alt + Tab view. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/snap-your-windows), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Some apps may not show snap layouts. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044681/), T4)
- A Snap Group is formed when multiple windows are snapped together using Snap Layouts. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/windows/windows-11/253108/windows-11-feature-focus-snap-groups), T4)
- The article discusses using Snap Layouts and Snap Groups on one display or across multiple displays, including docked scenarios. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/windows/windows-11/253108/windows-11-feature-focus-snap-groups), T4)
- At the time of writing, the feature was not fully baked. The article says it should improve to remember Snap Layouts and provide Snap Groups shortcuts after reboots and whether or not the system is docked. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/windows/windows-11/253108/windows-11-feature-focus-snap-groups), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions use the search label [Snap settings] rather than [Snap Groups setting]. They describe turning on [Snap windows] and snapping windows by dragging them to a hotspot; they do not describe Snap Groups. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1044681/), T4)
- The article says Snap Groups builds on Snap, a capability used in Windows for years; Snap Layouts and Snap Groups together represent what the author considers the biggest changes to Snap since Windows 8.1. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/windows/windows-11/253108/windows-11-feature-focus-snap-groups), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > Multitasking > Snap windows ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/snap-your-windows), T1)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + Z` — View available grid layout options (Windows 11). ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Left arrow` — Snap a window to the left half of the screen (Windows 11 or Windows 10). ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Right arrow` — Snap a window to the right half of the screen (Windows 11 or Windows 10). ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- `Windows key + left arrow` — Moves the current focus window to the left. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + right arrow` — Moves a window to the right. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + left arrow, then Windows key + right arrow + down arrow, then Windows key + right arrow + top arrow` — The article gives this sequence for snapping three windows: left, bottom-right, then top-right. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + left arrow + top arrow` — Snaps a window into the top-left corner. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + right arrow + down arrow` — The article also gives this as a way to snap a window into the bottom-right corner. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + top arrow` — Snaps a single app as a maximized window. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + down arrow` — Minimizes the window. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows key + Z` — Opens the Snap Layouts menu; choose a number for a layout, then press a number to place the app in a zone and continue snapping other windows. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- `Alt+Tab` — The article says snapped-window previews can be shown when pressing Alt+Tab, controlled by the corresponding Snap windows option. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The article says up to four windows can be snapped in four different layouts. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- To snap up to three windows in a vertical orientation, use Snap Layouts. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- Snap Layouts shown from the Maximize button or by dragging to the top of the screen depend on their respective settings being enabled. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- No SKU, hardware, region, Insider, or rollout limitations are stated. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- The number of Snap layouts depends on screen size. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/whats-new-multitasking-windows-11), T4)
- On a tablet in portrait mode, snapping to the right and left sides positions one window at the bottom and the other at the top. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/whats-new-multitasking-windows-11), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions describe dragging a window to the left or right edge to snap it to that half of the screen. The Windows 11 instructions describe hovering over the maximize button or using Windows logo key + Z to view layout options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/0d259fd9-e9d0-702c-c027-007f0e78eaf2), T1)
- The article says Snap Assist has been available since Windows 7; Windows 7 offered only snapping two windows side by side. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- The article says Windows 10 improved Snap Assist to support up to four snaps. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- The article says Windows 11 adds Snap Layouts for visual guidance and Snap Groups for returning to previously snapped windows. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- The article says the previous Snap assist experience supported around three different layouts; Snap layouts offers up to six, depending on screen size. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/whats-new-multitasking-windows-11), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > Multitasking > Snap windows ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/how-use-snap-assist-windows-11), T4)
- Settings > Multitasking ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/whats-new-multitasking-windows-11), T4)
