Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key+Up Arrow` — Maximize the window. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Shift+Windows key+Up Arrow` — Resize the window to full screen height without changing its width. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Windows key+Down Arrow` — Restore a maximized or full-height window; minimize a restored window. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Windows key+Left Arrow` — Snap the window to the left half of the screen. Repeated presses cycle through left, right, and restored positions; with multiple monitors, the positions cycle on each monitor in turn. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Windows key+Right Arrow` — Snap the window to the right half of the screen. Repeated presses cycle through left, right, and restored positions; with multiple monitors, the positions cycle on each monitor in turn. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Windows key+Home` — Minimize all windows except the active window; press again to restore windows previously minimized with this shortcut. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Windows key+M` — Minimize all windows. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- `Shift+Windows key+M` — Restore windows after minimizing. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Title Bar Window Shake may need to be turned On in Settings > System > Multitasking if it is not working. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- The page states that window snapping works with multimonitor setups; it does not specify a SKU, region, or rollout limitation for the requested features. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Aero Shake was introduced with Windows Vista and survives in Windows 11. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- The page says window-snapping techniques have been available for several Windows versions; Windows 11 expands the options. ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)
- Windows 10 extended window snapping to quadrants. When a window is snapped to half the screen, the user is prompted to select a second window for the other half. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Aero), T4)
- Windows 10 refers to Aero Shake as “Title bar window shake.” ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Aero), T4)
- In Windows 7, dragging a window to the left or right edge fills that half of the screen, and snapping it to the top maximizes it. Quickly shaking a window minimizes the others; shaking it again restores them. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Aero), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > Multitasking ([microsoftpressstore.com](https://www.microsoftpressstore.com/articles/article.aspx?p=3178893&seqNum=7), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Color customization is ignored when the app runs on Windows 10. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Title bar color customization support can be checked with AppWindowTitleBar.IsCustomizationSupported(). ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- PreferredHeightOption can be set to Tall only after ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is true; otherwise an exception is thrown. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- For custom title bars, interactive-region rectangles need to account for display scaling. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Full-screen and compact-overlay modes are available only if supported by the app. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Applies to Windows App SDK and WinUI 3 desktop apps; the page does not state SKU, hardware, region, or Insider/rollout restrictions. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- Color customization is ignored when the app runs on Windows 10. IsCustomizationSupported returns true on Windows 10 starting with Windows App SDK 1.2, and on all Windows App SDK versions on Windows 11; the page separately states that color customization has no effect on Windows 10. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- Transparent caption-button background colors are supported only when ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is true. If it is false, alpha is ignored for all AppWindowTitleBar color properties. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- Only ButtonBackgroundColor, ButtonHoverBackgroundColor, ButtonPressedBackgroundColor, and ButtonInactiveBackgroundColor can use transparency when content extends into the title bar. Other color properties ignore alpha. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- PreferredHeightOption is supported only for a fully custom title bar; ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar must be true before setting it. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- AppWindow uses physical pixels. WinUI 3 and WPF values need display-scale adjustment when the display is not at 100%. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- The system caption-button area does not receive app UI input; content may be drawn underneath it but should not be interactive. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Setting Window.ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar in XAML causes an error; set it in code. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Transparent colors cannot be set for the simple/default title bar customization; the alpha channel is ignored. For a fully customized title bar, alpha is supported for the listed caption-button background color properties. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- When ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is false, the alpha channel is ignored for all AppWindowTitleBar color properties. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- The Close button does not use the configured button background color for hover and pressed states. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- The system caption-button area does not receive input for app UI placed beneath it. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- The page does not describe confirmation dialogs. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- Setting PreferredHeightOption while ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar is false throws an exception. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- Transparent colors cannot be set for title-bar color properties generally; alpha is ignored except for the specified caption-button background properties under the stated condition. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10: title bar color customization is ignored; the page says color customization is not supported there. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Windows App SDK 1.4 and later: XAML Window and AppWindow use the same AppWindowTitleBar object for title bar customization. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- For apps not using WinUI 1.3 or later, the page describes using interop APIs to obtain AppWindow. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar), T1)
- Windows 10: title-bar color customization is ignored, even though IsCustomizationSupported returns true starting with Windows App SDK 1.2. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)
- The page does not state differences for Windows 7. ([github.com](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-dev-docs/blob/docs/hub/apps/develop/title-bar.md), T2)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + Shift + Right arrow` — Move an app to a monitor on the right. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Shift + Left arrow` — Move an app to a monitor on the left. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/save-time-with-keyboard-shortcuts-3a5931a4-b904-7295-ab39-0b80e596b75e), T1)
- `Win + Left` — Moves the active window to the left half of the screen; pressing the arrow again snaps it into a quarter. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/how-to-use-windows-11-keyboard-shortcuts/), T1)
- `Win + Right` — Moves the active window to the right half of the screen; pressing the arrow again snaps it into a quarter. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/how-to-use-windows-11-keyboard-shortcuts/), T1)
- `Win + Left Arrow` — Snap window left. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)
- `Win + Right Arrow` — Snap window right. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)
- `Win + Left Arrow, then Win + Up Arrow` — Snap window to the top-left corner. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)
- `Win + Right Arrow, then Win + Up Arrow` — Snap window to the top-right corner. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)
- `Win + Left Arrow, then Win + Down Arrow` — Snap window to the bottom-left corner. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)
- `Win + Right Arrow, then Win + Down Arrow` — Snap window to the bottom-right corner. ([pctips.com](https://www.pctips.com/snap-windows/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win+I` — Opens Settings. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Only widgets that support a small size can be added to the lock screen. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-lock-screen-in-windows), T1)
- Widget customization is available only if the widget provider supports it. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-lock-screen-in-windows), T1)
- Lock-screen widget content might be tailored using location estimation. This can come from Windows Location service, if enabled; otherwise, it might use the internet connection's IP address. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-lock-screen-in-windows), T1)
- The change began rolling out to new users in July 2026 and is gradually rolling out to existing users; availability varies by device. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)
- The KB5120998 page applies to Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, all editions. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)
- Lock-screen widget content may be tailored using estimated location: Windows Location service data if that service is on, or the internet connection’s IP address if it is off. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)
- The four-widget maximum is attributed to a community guide, not Microsoft support. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)
- The page says the widgets arrive with the March 2024 optional update. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2024/03/22/windows-11-lock-screen-gets-msn-weather-sports-money-integration/amp/), T4)
- The page says the feature is enabled by default for consumers in the April 2024 Patch Tuesday update. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2024/03/22/windows-11-lock-screen-gets-msn-weather-sports-money-integration/amp/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page's Windows 10 section describes choosing one app for detailed lock-screen status and selecting apps for quick status; the Windows 11 section describes a Widgets list instead. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-lock-screen-in-windows), T1)
- The page says similar features were first added in Windows 10 and that the widgets appear at the bottom of the lock screen in both versions. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2024/03/22/windows-11-lock-screen-gets-msn-weather-sports-money-integration/amp/), T4)
- The page says Windows 11 places the clock and time at the top of the lock screen, describing this as better alignment. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2024/03/22/windows-11-lock-screen-gets-msn-weather-sports-money-integration/amp/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > Personalization > Lock screen ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/personalization/customize-the-lock-screen-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Personalization > Lock screen ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-lock-screen-widgets-weather-only-default-kb5120998-timeline-and-customization.446976/), T5)
- Settings > Personalization > Lock Screen > Lock Screen Status ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2024/03/22/windows-11-lock-screen-gets-msn-weather-sports-money-integration/amp/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The availability of certain settings may vary based on the device configuration. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/security/sign-in-options-in-windows), T1)
- Enhanced Sign-in Security is available only on devices with compatible hardware. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/security/sign-in-options-in-windows), T1)
- Passkeys are not mentioned. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/security/sign-in-options-in-windows), T1)
- Passkeys can be used with websites and apps that support them. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The Windows editions listed as supporting passkeys are Windows Pro, Windows Enterprise, Windows Pro Education/SE, and Windows Education; the page lists corresponding passkey license entitlements. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- Cross-device authentication requires Bluetooth enabled on both the Windows and mobile devices, Internet connectivity, and proximity for the described phone/tablet flows. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The linked-device option is supported only for Android devices. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The page says Microsoft Entra ID passkeys can't currently be stored on Windows devices. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The device must have a screen lock set up; passkeys will not work without a PIN, face, or fingerprint configured. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- On Windows 11 version 24H2, apps must ask for consent before using passkeys. If consent was declined, the page directs users to Settings > Privacy & security > Passkey access. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- Passkeys work on Windows 10 and Windows 11, according to the page. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- The page states no SKU, Copilot+ PC, region, or Insider-channel requirement. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The Windows-device creation flow asks the user to select OK after Windows Hello verification and again to confirm the passkey was saved. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- Security-key creation asks the user to select OK to confirm setup and again after the passkey is saved. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- Some passkeys for login.microsoft.com can't be deleted because they're used with Microsoft Entra ID and/or Microsoft Account for signing in to the device and Microsoft services. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- Passkey creation is confirmed with a PIN or biometric. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- “No passkeys available” may mean the device screen lock is not set up. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- “This passkey can no longer be used” may mean the passkey was deleted or the PIN or biometric setup changed; the page says to create a new one. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- “Something went wrong” may be caused by a timeout or trying to save a second passkey for the same site in a synced manager. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section does not list Sign in with an external camera or fingerprint reader; that setting is listed in the Windows 11 section. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/security/sign-in-options-in-windows), T1)
- Passkeys can be used in all supported versions of Windows clients. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The native Settings experience for viewing and managing passkeys starts with Windows 11, version 22H2 with KB5030310. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The page applies to Windows 10 and Windows 11; it states no Windows 7 behavior. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- The page says passkeys work on both Windows 10 and Windows 11. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- The built-in Settings page for viewing and managing passkeys is stated to start with Windows 11 version 22H2 and KB5030310. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Accounts > Sign-in options ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/security/sign-in-options-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Accounts > Passkeys ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/passkeys/?tabs=windows), T1)
- Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- Settings > Accounts > Passkeys > Advanced options ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)
- Settings > Privacy & security > Passkey access ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-10-11-passkeys-set-up-windows-hello-syncing-and-lost-pc-recovery.446199/), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + X` — Opens a menu with Shut down or sign out > Hibernate. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Hibernate is not available on all PCs; the page gives PCs with InstantGo as an example that do not have the Hibernate option. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Hibernate is described as designed for laptops and suggested for extended periods without an opportunity to charge the battery. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- The lid setting applies to laptops. Power-button behavior may be configured for desktops, tablets, or laptops. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Wake behavior varies by PC; the page advises checking the computer documentation or manufacturer's website. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page does not describe a confirmation prompt or error for shutting down, sleeping, or hibernating. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- If connected devices do not work properly after waking from Sleep or hibernate, the page suggests disconnecting and reconnecting them or restarting the PC, and checking that drivers are current. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- The guide addresses a missing Hibernate option and says to confirm that Hibernate appears in the power menu after enabling it. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fhaDEXB1KOA), T4)
- Hibernate saves open apps and files to the hard drive and fully powers off the PC; the guide contrasts this with Sleep, which still draws a small amount of power to keep the session in memory. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fhaDEXB1KOA), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions use Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings to open power options; the Windows 11 instructions use Search > control panel > System and Security > Power Options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Windows 10 hibernation instructions specify selecting the Hibernate checkbox under Shutdown settings, if available. The Windows 11 instructions say to select Hibernate under Shutdown settings. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- No Windows 7 differences are stated. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Power > Shut down ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Search > control panel > System and Security > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Start > Power > Hibernate ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Windows logo key + X > Shut down or sign out > Hibernate ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/power-battery/shut-down-sleep-or-hibernate-your-pc), T1)
- Control Panel > System and Security > Power Options > Change what the power buttons do > Shutdown settings ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Ww0WuzSnQg), T4)

- The restart flow described occurs after the Windows 11 upgrade’s installation portion is done in Windows 10. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ways-to-install-windows-11-e0edbbfb-cfc5-4011-868b-2ce77ac7c70e?nochrome=), T1)

- The change allowing shutdown or restart without installing pending updates is still being tested and is not live outside the Windows Insider Program. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/27/tested-microsoft-fixes-the-windows-11-trap-that-installs-updates-when-you-just-want-to-shut-down-or-reboot-pc/), T4)
- The author tested the behavior in a virtual machine with a driver update that required a reboot. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/27/tested-microsoft-fixes-the-windows-11-trap-that-installs-updates-when-you-just-want-to-shut-down-or-reboot-pc/), T4)
- The fix is stated to apply to supported Windows 11 builds: 24H2 Build 26100.7019 or later, or 25H2 Build 26200.7019 or later. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)
- The fix first appeared in optional KB5067036 for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, and was included in the November 2025 Patch Tuesday cumulative update. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)
- No SKU, hardware, region, or Insider-specific limits are stated. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page reports that the former behavior could force-install important pending updates even when Shut down or Restart was selected. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/27/tested-microsoft-fixes-the-windows-11-trap-that-installs-updates-when-you-just-want-to-shut-down-or-reboot-pc/), T4)
- The page reports that the Update & shut down bug fix rolled out in October 2025. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/04/27/tested-microsoft-fixes-the-windows-11-trap-that-installs-updates-when-you-just-want-to-shut-down-or-reboot-pc/), T4)
- Before the fix, Windows sometimes treated Update and shut down as a normal restart and returned to the login screen. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)
- The page says Windows has corrected this behavior in the specified Windows 11 builds. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The issue also affected Windows 10, but the page says the correction has only been delivered to supported Windows 11 builds. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)
- The page does not state differences for Windows 7. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ways-to-install-windows-11-e0edbbfb-cfc5-4011-868b-2ce77ac7c70e?nochrome=), T1)
- Settings → Windows Update ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)
- Settings → System → About ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows/windows-11-finally-fixes-the-long-broken-update-and-shut-down-option-that-has-plagued-me-for-years), T4)

- The command's behavior is build-dependent; the page discusses 24H2, 25H2, and newer builds and says newer builds may block it. ([github.com](https://github.com/codewithelmor/Microslop-Setup/blob/main/Windows-11-Local-Account-Install-Guide.md), T2)

- The page says illustrations may vary depending on device model or system version. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1041493/), T4)

- The guide says a restart of the installation may be simpler than resetting OOBE. ([github.com](https://github.com/codewithelmor/Microslop-Setup/blob/main/Windows-11-Local-Account-Install-Guide.md), T2)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- For Windows 10, the page says to select a keyboard layout; for Windows 11, it says keyboard layout or input method. Both instructions say to select a region or country and click [Yes], then select the keyboard option and click [Yes]. Both describe Add layout for adding a second keyboard layout and [Skip] otherwise. ([asus.com](https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1041493/), T4)

- The page states no hardware, region, Insider, or rollout conditions. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/get-connected-when-setting-up-your-windows-device), T1)
- The page claims the OOBE bypass mechanism no longer works and that Rufus cannot bypass the Microsoft account requirement; it also includes conflicting reports that offline setup or local account creation still works on 25H2. ([linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/faizan-ahmed-07a7aa33_heads-up-for-all-it-officers-admins-just-activity-7393527235581931521-e4wv), T4)
- One commenter says 24H2 is the last build where the bypass still works. ([linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/faizan-ahmed-07a7aa33_heads-up-for-all-it-officers-admins-just-activity-7393527235581931521-e4wv), T4)
- A commenter says they had not tested the latest build and that not connecting to a network might still work. ([linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/faizan-ahmed-07a7aa33_heads-up-for-all-it-officers-admins-just-activity-7393527235581931521-e4wv), T4)
- A commenter reports successfully using an offline account on Windows 11 25H2 Enterprise with Rufus. ([linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/faizan-ahmed-07a7aa33_heads-up-for-all-it-officers-admins-just-activity-7393527235581931521-e4wv), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page says Microsoft removed the obvious “I don’t have internet” or “Skip for now” options during OOBE starting with Windows 11 22H2 and continuing through 24H2. ([triplescomputers.com](https://triplescomputers.com/blog/everythingelse/solution-skip-microsoft-account-requirement-during-windows-11-24h2-fresh-install/), T4)
- The page says `oobe\bypassnro` does not work on recent releases/updates and gives `start ms-cxh:localonly` as an alternative. ([triplescomputers.com](https://triplescomputers.com/blog/everythingelse/solution-skip-microsoft-account-requirement-during-windows-11-24h2-fresh-install/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page applies to both Windows 10 and Windows 11; it states no differences between them. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/get-connected-when-setting-up-your-windows-device), T1)

- After OOBE, through Settings > Accounts — [cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Shift + F10` — Opens Command Prompt during OOBE on supported screens. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- `Fn + Shift + F10` — Alternative for some laptops to open Command Prompt during OOBE. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- `Windows key + R` — Opens Run so the user can enter `winver` to identify the Windows build. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- `Ctrl + Shift + J` — Reported on some preview builds to open an OOBE developer console; unsupported and build-dependent. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- `Windows + R` — Open Run after Windows is running; enter `winver` to check edition and build. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page says a local account may have been chosen during initial device setup, but it does not describe an OOBE Microsoft account requirement or OOBE local-account paths. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/manage/change-from-a-local-account-to-a-microsoft-account-in-windows), T1)
- The account-switching links are shown only for the corresponding account type: the Microsoft-account link for a local account, and the local-account link for a Microsoft account. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/manage/change-from-a-local-account-to-a-microsoft-account-in-windows), T1)
- Windows 11 Home, Pro, Enterprise, and Education do not necessarily expose the same setup choices. “Domain join instead” is generally a Pro or other non-Home option, not a normal Home option. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page reports `start ms-cxh:localonly` on some Windows 11 25H2 retail media, but says it is undocumented and removed or blocked in some Insider builds. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- `OOBEBYPASSNRO` may work on older 24H2 or earlier installation media; some newer 25H2 images and Insider builds may not include the script or may disable the behavior. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page identifies 25H2 build 26200.8875 and 24H2 build 26100.8875 as July 14, 2026 general-availability builds, and says cumulative updates can change exact builds. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page says 26H1 is a separate, platform-specific branch for selected silicon and warns not to assume a 25H2 command works on it. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- OEM recovery images, Insider builds, edition, network state, and downloaded OOBE updates can change the screens and available options. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The Rufus local-account path requires the target PC to be unable to reach the network during the relevant OOBE step; the page recommends disconnecting Ethernet and not joining Wi-Fi. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- For devices enrolled in Autopilot, Intune, Microsoft Entra ID, or other organizational management, the page directs users to the organization, seller, or authorized administrator rather than evading enrollment. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- These account paths do not bypass Windows activation, licensing, TPM, or Secure Boot requirements. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page notes that Rufus’s local-account answer-file option can conflict with Windows S Mode. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page recommends creating a password reset disk for a local account; if the password is forgotten without one, the password cannot be recovered. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/manage/change-from-a-local-account-to-a-microsoft-account-in-windows), T1)
- Don't use the SkipMachineOOBE setting to automate OOBE. Instead, use the above unattend settings. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/automate-oobe?view=windows-11), T1)
- Rufus warns that preparing the USB can erase it; the page says to confirm the correct USB device before proceeding. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- A clean installation can erase target-disk partitions and the OEM recovery environment; the page recommends backing up data first. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page says the OOBE commands and registry values are undocumented or build-dependent and may fail even when entered successfully. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- If offline options do not appear after a real network disconnection and restart, the page recommends changing methods rather than repeatedly running the command. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The page says not to use these methods to evade organizational management or enrollment. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- Rufus warns that selecting the USB device and starting media creation erases that USB drive. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The article warns that a clean installation can erase Windows partitions, recovery partitions, applications, and personal files. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- If `OOBEBYPASSNRO` is not recognized, the article lists a removed script, keyboard-layout changes, mistyping, or a newer Insider image as possible causes. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- If `start ms-cxh:localonly` does nothing, the article says it may be unavailable on the build or may have been run at the wrong OOBE screen. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- The article says `ipconfig /release` alone is less reliable than physically disconnecting Ethernet or otherwise disabling network access. ([cloudspress.com](https://www.cloudspress.com/how-to-create-a-local-account-in-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page applies to both Windows 11 and Windows 10; it states no differences between them and gives no Windows 7 information. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/manage/change-from-a-local-account-to-a-microsoft-account-in-windows), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings app > Accounts > Your info ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accounts-billing/manage/change-from-a-local-account-to-a-microsoft-account-in-windows), T1)
- Unattended Windows Setup Reference ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/automate-oobe?view=windows-11), T1)
- Automate Windows Setup ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/automate-oobe?view=windows-11), T1)
- Windows Auto Pilot ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/automate-oobe?view=windows-11), T1)
- Settings > Accounts > Your info ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)
- Settings > Accounts > Other users ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-bypass-a-microsoft-account-during-windows-11-oobe-methods-that-still-work-in-2026/), T4)

| WA.11.05.i01 | During setup of a new PC or after reinstalling Windows, sign in with the Microsoft account used to make the backup. | Windows detects the backup and asks whether to restore one. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup) |
| WA.11.05.i02 | If more than one PC is backed up, select More options, then select the backup to restore. | The selected backup is restored; the page says the items will be there when the user reaches the desktop. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup) |
| WA.11.05.i03 | Select an app pin for an app available in the Microsoft Store. | The app can be restored. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup) |
| WA.11.05.i04 | Select an app pin for an app unavailable in the Microsoft Store. | Windows directs the user to the web to download the installer. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup) |
| WA.11.05.i05 | Sign in to OneDrive with the Microsoft account used for the original backup. | Files are available. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup) |
| WA.11.05.i06 | Select the device from which to restore data | Choose the device whose OneDrive backup will be restored. | T4 | [dell.com](https://www.dell.com/support/contents/en-sv/videos/videoplayer/how-to-backup-and-restore-dell-support-for-windows-11/6323134951112) |
| WA.11.05.i07 | Click Next | Continue through the on-screen instructions to complete the restore process. | T4 | [dell.com](https://www.dell.com/support/contents/en-sv/videos/videoplayer/how-to-backup-and-restore-dell-support-for-windows-11/6323134951112) |
| WA.11.05.i08 | During initial setup of a new or reset PC, sign in with the same Microsoft account used on the old PC and choose the old device profile. | Windows can bring back the pieces it knows about, including selected settings, preferences, an app list, and OneDrive-synced files. Apps may need to be reinstalled manually. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/) |
| WA.11.05.i09 | Complete setup without using the restore experience. | The coordinated return of apps, settings, and preferences is not available later through an ordinary consumer-facing “restore my Windows Backup now” button. OneDrive files remain accessible as cloud-synced files. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/) |

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The user must sign in with the same Microsoft account used to make the backup. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup), T1)
- The page says Windows Backup is focused on consumer devices using a personal Microsoft account; work or school Microsoft accounts won't work. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup), T1)
- The page does not state SKU, hardware, region, or Insider/rollout limits for OOBE restore. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup), T1)
- The settings and OneDrive folders must be synced. ([dell.com](https://www.dell.com/support/contents/en-sv/videos/videoplayer/how-to-backup-and-restore-dell-support-for-windows-11/6323134951112), T4)
- Backups must have been created using OneDrive. ([dell.com](https://www.dell.com/support/contents/en-sv/videos/videoplayer/how-to-backup-and-restore-dell-support-for-windows-11/6323134951112), T4)
- The consumer restore experience occurs during initial Windows setup on a new or reset PC. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- The user signs in with the same Microsoft account and chooses the old device profile. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- OneDrive storage limits apply to synced files. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- The article describes a separate Windows Backup for Organizations scenario: restore may be integrated into OOBE or first sign-in on supported Windows 11 builds and joined-device scenarios. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The restore experience is tied to setup; the article says there is no ordinary consumer-facing way to invoke the coordinated restore later from the desktop. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- The app list is not a copy of installed programs; desktop applications may require manual reinstallation and may need licensing, drivers, or other components. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- Files outside protected OneDrive-synced locations are not covered by that file component. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page applies to Windows 10 and Windows 11 but states no OOBE restore differences between them. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup), T1)
- The page says Windows 10 support ended on October 14, 2025; it does not describe a Windows 10 OOBE restore difference. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/backup-recovery/back-up-and-restore-with-windows-backup), T1)
- The page describes restoring from a synced Windows 10 system when migrating to Windows 11. ([dell.com](https://www.dell.com/support/contents/en-sv/videos/videoplayer/how-to-backup-and-restore-dell-support-for-windows-11/6323134951112), T4)
- The article says “Backup and Restore (Windows 7)” remains in Windows 11; it does not describe this as the OOBE restore feature. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)
- The article mentions File History as a separate legacy Control Panel feature for versioned file copies, not as the coordinated OOBE restore. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Accounts > Windows backup ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-backup-is-really-migration-what-it-does-and-what-it-doesnt.427387/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The credential prompt is the default for standard users. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- The consent prompt is the default for administrator accounts in Admin Approval Mode. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Administrators can be required to provide credentials by setting the elevation-prompt policy to Prompt for credentials. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Consent and credential prompts are displayed on the secure desktop by default; the article recommends keeping the secure-desktop policy enabled. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Prompt behavior depends on security policies. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Administrator prompt behavior applies to administrators in Admin Approval Mode; standard-user prompt behavior applies to standard users. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration), T1)
- With Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation enabled, all elevation requests go to the secure desktop regardless of the administrator and standard-user prompt behavior policies. When disabled, requests go to the interactive user's desktop and those prompt behavior policies are used. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration), T1)
- Automatically deny elevation requests displays a configurable access denied error message. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration), T1)
- Which prompt appears depends on the kind of account being used: members of the Administrators group see a consent prompt; standard users see a credential prompt by default. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page does not specify what selecting Deny does. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration), T1)
- For standard users, Automatically deny elevation requests displays a configurable access denied error message. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page recommends enabling the secure-desktop policy setting for higher security. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- The clipboard-paste restriction is stated for Windows Server 2019 onward and is described as matching currently supported Windows client OS versions. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- The secure desktop policy is enabled by default. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)
- The no-dimming slider option displays prompts on the normal desktop and is not recommended by Microsoft. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)
- The clipboard restriction is stated for Windows Server 2019 and supported Windows client versions. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The secure desktop is intended to prevent other programs from tampering with the elevation prompt. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)
- The article warns that a fake credential prompt could harvest a password; it advises entering administrator credentials only when you initiated the action. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Starting in Windows Server 2019, clipboard content cannot be pasted on the secure desktop; the page says this matches currently supported Windows client OS versions. No Windows 10 or Windows 7 comparison is stated. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Windows 8/8.1: when UAC is triggered, all applications and the taskbar are hidden while the desktop is dimmed. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Account_Control), T4)
- Windows 11 is described as having mostly the same UAC layout as later Windows 10 versions, with visual changes matching the operating system’s look and feel. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Account_Control), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/keep-secure/how-user-account-control-works), T1)
- Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation is under Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options in Local Security Policy. ([dev.to](https://dev.to/mfaysaldev/what-is-uac-in-windows-user-account-control-explained-for-beginners-3lg0), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Supported editions: Windows 11 Home, Pro, Enterprise, and Education. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- Available with KB5120998. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- Applies to supported Windows 11 devices, excluding Windows 365 Cloud PCs and Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts; support for those environments and Windows Server editions is planned for a future release. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The Windows Security option is currently available in the Windows Insider Program as a preview and is rolling out gradually. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- A reboot is required for Administrator protection to take effect. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The page advises not enabling the feature on Windows 365 Cloud PCs, Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, devices that require Hyper-V, devices using apps that access shared files across profiles, or devices managed with Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS). ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The page says Windows security baselines enable Administrator protection by default with the October 2026 Windows security update; the stated baselines cover Windows 11 versions 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- For Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, the page recommends configuring users as standard users. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- When Administrator protection is enabled, remote-logon behavior depends on the stated remote-logon policies. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The article says the feature is being delivered through Insider Preview channels and that preview or Canary behavior may differ from the eventual general-availability implementation. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)
- The article says devices that require Hyper-V or Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) may not be suitable for Administrator Protection. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)
- The article notes that unsigned or blocked legacy drivers may fail to load, and that SSO or network-resource workflows may require changes. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Windows Security prompts for a restart after the toggle is turned on. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The page states that a reboot is required after enabling or disabling the feature through policy. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- Event ID 15031 records an approved elevation; Event ID 15032 records an elevation that is denied, fails, or times out. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The page reports that non-admin RDP logons can fail with error 0xC000000D after KB5124010 on devices with Administrator protection enabled; the stated workaround is to turn off Administrator protection by resetting the User Account Control Type of Admin Approval Mode policy through Intune or Group Policy. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The article describes interactive authorization for each administrative operation, typically using Windows Hello; it does not provide a specific prompt label or error message. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)
- It warns that some elevated installs may not place shortcuts in the Start menu and that elevated apps may not have access to network drives or shared resources. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)
- The article says users must interactively authorize every admin operation. ([pcworld.com](https://www.pcworld.com/article/2848760/windows-11-battens-down-security-with-new-admin-rights-check-feature.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page states that setting User Account Control: Configure type of Admin Approval Mode to Legacy Admin Approval Mode (Default) disables Administrator protection. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- When the remote-logon policy is enabled, elevated remote logons match traditional UAC behavior. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)
- The article contrasts Administrator Protection with UAC, saying UAC relied on prompts and users could become habituated to clicking through; it does not state specific Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-administrator-protection-just-in-time-elevation-and-isolation.401218/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- LocalPoliciesSecurityOptions CSP ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/?tabs=intune), T1)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win+R` — Opens the Run dialog for entering regedit. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- `Win+I` — Opens Windows Settings. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- `Enter` — Submits regedit in the Run dialog. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The Privacy page does not list apps that have permission to use all system resources; Windows Desktop apps fall into this category. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/app-permissions), T1)
- The page says most permissions for apps with access to all system resources cannot be controlled in Settings > Privacy. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/app-permissions), T1)
- Students using Windows 11 SE cannot download apps from Microsoft Store; apps are managed by their IT Admin. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/app-permissions), T1)
- The page says apps should not assume a sensitive resource is always available. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)
- The page recommends declaring privacy-sensitive capabilities even for Medium IL apps so they can be managed in privacy settings pages as soon as they are installed. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)
- A webcam app also needs the microphone capability to access the audio stream. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)
- The page says the feature is available after updating to Build 25977 or later. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- The feature was released in Windows Insider Builds; rollout to stable versions was expected. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- Administrative privileges may be needed to adjust location-access permissions. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- The page recommends backing up the registry before making changes. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- The page says some apps may not work properly until the notification setting is enabled if they are blocked from accessing location. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- The notification or prompt behavior is described for apps requesting location while Location Services is off. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/enable-or-disable-location-services-in-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- When using regedit, the page says to click Yes in the User Account Control prompt. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)
- The page warns that disabling Notify when apps request location means Windows will no longer notify you if an app is blocked from accessing your current location. ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10: Start > Settings > Privacy; select an app, such as Calendar, and choose which permissions are on or off. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/app-permissions), T1)
- The page distinguishes AppContainer apps from Medium IL (full trust) apps. It says some capabilities apply only to AppContainer apps, while privacy-sensitive capabilities are recommended for Medium IL apps too. It does not state Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > Privacy & security ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/app-permissions), T1)
- Windows Settings privacy settings pages ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)
- Settings charm ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations), T1)
- Settings > Privacy & security > App permissions > Location ([thewindowsclub.com](https://www.thewindowsclub.com/notify-when-apps-request-location-in-windows-11), T4)

| `location` | Device capability for access to location functionality. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations) |
| `microphone` | Device capability for access to the microphone audio feed. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations) |
| `webcam` | Device capability for access to a camera's video feed. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations) |
| `Windows.Devices.Geolocation` | Mentioned in the page as the supported APIs to use for location-related scenarios in place of the removed `locationHistory` capability. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + E` — Opens File Explorer. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/folder-suggestions-in-windows-10-698df84b-0a81-bebb-f90e-ee0da943751a), T1)
- `Windows key + E` — Open File Explorer. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- `Ctrl + C` — Copy selected photo(s). ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- `Ctrl + V` — Paste into the destination folder. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- `Ctrl + X` — Cut the selected photo. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- `F2` — Rename the selected photo. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- `Enter` — Confirm a new photo name or submit a search. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Requires a PC running Windows 11. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- Gallery may be missing until Windows is updated; the page recommends checking for updates and restarting. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- Photos must be in accessible locations; cloud-based files should be available and synced. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- The page lists JPG, JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, and TIFF as common supported image formats. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- The page states no SKU, hardware, region, Insider, or rollout-specific limits. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- Deleting a photo from Gallery may delete the original file from its actual folder. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- Removing a folder from the collection does not delete that folder or its photos. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- The page says to confirm a folder removal if prompted. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)
- If a photo is deleted by mistake, check the Recycle Bin, OneDrive recycle bin if applicable, or available backups. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page states that Quick access was renamed to File Explorer Home in Windows 11, version 22H2. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/folder-suggestions-in-windows-10-698df84b-0a81-bebb-f90e-ee0da943751a), T1)
- The Windows 10 context-menu commands remain available in Windows 11 through Show more options; not all Windows 10 extensions are available in the streamlined Windows 11 context menu. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/folder-suggestions-in-windows-10-698df84b-0a81-bebb-f90e-ee0da943751a), T1)
- The page says File Explorer is identical to previous versions, while identifying “Home” and “Gallery” as notable new features. It does not specify Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences. ([helpcenter.ccac.edu](https://helpcenter.ccac.edu/microsoft-windows/windows-11-guide), T4)
- The page states Gallery is not a Windows 10 File Explorer feature. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > Accounts — sign in to cloud accounts. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/folder-suggestions-in-windows-10-698df84b-0a81-bebb-f90e-ee0da943751a), T1)
- Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/use-windows-11-file-explorer-gallery-to-find-and-manage-photos-faster.435801/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page says Home replaced the page formerly called Quick access starting with Windows 11 version 22H2. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- The page says the known folders no longer appear in This PC from version 22H2. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- For Windows 10, the page says libraries do not show in File Explorer unless enabled; select the View tab > Navigation pane > Show libraries to add them to the left pane. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- The page says previous Windows versions used a plus sign next to a folder containing documents or subfolders; Windows 11 uses a right-pointing triangle for folders containing subfolders. ([it.environment.ucdavis.edu](https://it.environment.ucdavis.edu/file-explorer), T4)
- Starting with Windows 11 version 22H2, Home replaced the former Quick access start page; Quick access is now the pinned section inside Home and the navigation pane. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- From version 22H2, known folders no longer appear in This PC. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Windows 11 address-bar input compatibility is specified for build 26300.8376 (Experimental), build 26220.8680 (Beta 25H2), build 26100.8728 (RP 24H2), and build 26200.8728 (RP 25H2). - Those Windows 11 builds support paths containing double backslashes and quotation marks; the page gives C:\Users\user and "C:\Users\user" as examples. ([elevenforum.com](https://www.elevenforum.com/t/show-full-path-in-file-explorer-address-bar-in-windows-11.11038/), T5)
