Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows+E` — Opens File Explorer. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- `F6` — Moves focus forward through the main window elements, including the tab control. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- `Shift+F6` — Moves focus backward through the main window elements, including the tab control. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- `Tab` — Moves between elements within the toolbar, app bar, and Add a new tab. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- `Ctrl + T` — Open a new tab. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + Tab` — Move to the next tab. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + Shift + Tab` — Move to the previous tab. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 9` — Jump to the corresponding tab number. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + W` — Close the current tab. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 8` — Switch directly to the nth tab. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The article says there is no hard cap on open tabs; display and memory constraints are described as natural limits. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)
- No SKU, Copilot+ PC, region, Insider, or rollout restrictions are stated. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The article says session restore may intermittently fail after major system updates or hardware reconfigurations and advises against relying on it alone for mission-critical file sets. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The article states that native File Explorer tabs were not backported to Windows 10. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)
- Windows 7 is not discussed. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates; the article says new File Explorer features such as tabs reach the PC through Windows Update. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-use-file-explorer-in-windows-11.html), T4)
- Three-dot menu > Options > Folder Options > Restore previous folder windows at logon ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-file-explorer-tabs-boost-productivity-with-native-tabbed-navigation.370385/), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key E` — Opens File Explorer. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- `Windows key + E` — Open File Explorer. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/fix-missing-file-explorer-navigation-pane-in-windows-11-10.444520/), T5)
- `Alt` — Temporarily displays the classic menu bar while File Explorer is open. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page applies to Windows 11 and Windows 10; the Command Bar navigation-pane instructions are stated for Windows 11. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- Starting with Windows 11, version 22H2, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music, and Videos are pinned by default in Quick access. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- Not all extensions from Windows 10 are available in the streamlined Windows 11 context menu; the page says they are available through Show more options. Some apps may update over time to join the new context menu; check with the app developer for availability and timing. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- The page says the option to always show menus is not available in all Windows 11 editions or builds. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)
- The white-bar issue example is identified as Windows 11 Home Single Language, version 22H2, build 22621.2361, on a PC with an AMD Athlon Silver 3050U, integrated Radeon graphics, and 16 GB RAM. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If the pane does not return, close the Explorer window, open a new one, and repeat the check. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/fix-missing-file-explorer-navigation-pane-in-windows-11-10.444520/), T5)
- The page warns that modifying the registry carries risk and recommends making a backup or following an official Microsoft guide. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 context-menu commands can be accessed in Windows 11 by selecting Show more options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- For Windows 10, the page describes sharing files through the Share tab and Share button; the Windows 11 instructions refer to Share on the ribbon. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- The Windows 10 instructions for showing file name extensions, hidden files, and item check boxes use View > Options > Change folder and search options, then the View tab. The Windows 11 instructions use View > Show. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- Windows 10 uses View on the ribbon, then Navigation pane; Windows 11 places Navigation pane under View > Show in the redesigned command bar. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/fix-missing-file-explorer-navigation-pane-in-windows-11-10.444520/), T5)
- The page describes the classic ribbon and Quick Access Toolbar as appearing in many Explorer windows, especially versions before Windows 11's more minimalist interface. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)
- It says Windows 11 has reduced the classic ribbon and moved some options into the three-dot See more menu. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)
- It compares the temporarily displayed File, Edit, View, and Help menu bar to the one seen in Windows 7. ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- File Explorer > See more > Options > General > Open File Explorer in: ([pchardwarepro.com](https://www.pchardwarepro.com/en/Toolbar-in-Windows-File-Explorer:-A-Complete-Guide/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Alt + P` — Toggles the Preview pane on or off. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- `Alt+P` — Toggles the Preview pane on or off, as suggested by the advisor. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- `Alt+Shift+P` — Show or hide the details pane. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/keyboard-shortcuts-in-windows-dcc61a57-8ff0-cffe-9796-cb9706c75eec), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page mentions a NoPreviewPane policy as a possible reason the Preview pane cannot be toggled. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- The AI answer says the Details pane and Preview pane cannot be displayed at the same time. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- The advisor suggests checking for a work or school email under Access Work or School if the menu and shortcut do not work. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- The AI answer says NoPreviewPane may prevent toggling the Preview pane. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- The page does not state any SKU, hardware, region, or rollout conditions. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- The page notes that shortcut behavior may vary in different applications and that it lists default Windows shortcuts. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/keyboard-shortcuts-in-windows-dcc61a57-8ff0-cffe-9796-cb9706c75eec), T1)
- No SKU, hardware, region, or rollout conditions are stated. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/keyboard-shortcuts-in-windows-dcc61a57-8ff0-cffe-9796-cb9706c75eec), T1)
- All low-integrity preview handlers must forward all keystrokes to the host using IPreviewHandlerFrame::TranslateAccelerator. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/building-preview-handlers), T1)
- The host queries the handler for IPreviewHandlerVisuals. If supported, the host provides it with color, font, and text color. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/building-preview-handlers), T1)
- The Preview pane shows a preview only when one is available. ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-4nkvGC_SGE), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The question author says the Preview pane option is not visible when opening View in File Explorer. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- An answer suggests checking whether a work or school email is listed under Settings > Accounts > Access Work or School if the menu options do not work. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- The page presents two menu paths: View > Show > Preview Pane and View > Preview pane. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- The advisor asks whether Alt+P toggles the pane if the menu option is unavailable. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- IOleWindow::ContextSensitiveHelp should return E_NOTIMPL. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/building-preview-handlers), T1)
- IOleWindow::GetWindow returns S_OK with the handler window's HWND if the window exists; otherwise, it returns E_FAIL. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/building-preview-handlers), T1)
- After IPreviewHandler::Unload is called, the handler must be reinitialized before IPreviewHandler::DoPreview is called again. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/building-preview-handlers), T1)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page’s additional, older File Explorer shortcuts list describes Alt+P as “Display the preview panel” and does not list Alt+Shift+P for the details pane. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/keyboard-shortcuts-in-windows-dcc61a57-8ff0-cffe-9796-cb9706c75eec), T1)

Related Settings paths:

- File Explorer Options > View > Advanced settings > Show preview handlers in preview pane ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- Settings > Accounts > Access Work or School (suggested in the answer to check for a listed work or school email if the menu options do not work) ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/a/12979199), T5)
- Settings > Accounts > Access Work or School ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)
- File Explorer > Options > View ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/6018802/how-to-fix-preview-pane-on-my-pc), T5)

### WA.13.09 Search in File Explorer

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | PARTIAL — 1 T1/T2 and 2 T4/T5 sources relevant. Official sources are not specific to build 26300.9711; live-build check pending. |
| Applies to (as stated by sources) | Windows 11 (not build-specific); Windows 11 and Windows 10; the page does not specify a build or channel. |
| Relevant sources | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows) (T1), [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html) (T4), [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11) (T4) |
| Inspected, not relevant | 0 |
| Snippet-only candidates | 9 (register only) |

Entry points:

- Open File Explorer and search from Home, a drive, or a folder. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows)
- For a slow but in-depth search, search from This PC instead of Home. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows)
- Open File Explorer and search from the folder that most likely contains the file. — [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html)
- Open File Explorer at This PC to search across every drive. — [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html)
- On Windows 11, use Home in File Explorer to search across the PC and the cloud. — [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html)
- Open File Explorer with Windows key + E, browse to the location to search, and use the search box. — [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11)
- To search the entire computer rather than only known folders, open Settings > Privacy & security > Searching Windows. — [windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + E` — Open File Explorer. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + E` — Put the cursor in the File Explorer search box. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + F` — Jump to the File Explorer search box. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- `F3` — Jump to the File Explorer search box. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- `Enter` — Run the File Explorer search. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + Shift + 6` — Switch File Explorer to Details view. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Semantic indexing is described for Copilot+ PCs; supported document formats are .txt, .pdf, .docx, .doc, .rtf, .pptx, .ppt, .xls, and .xlsx; supported image formats are .jpg/.jpeg, .png, .gif, .bmp, and .ico. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- Semantic indexing data is stated to be stored locally on the PC, or locally in Cloud PC storage on AI-enabled Windows 365 devices. The page says it is not stored by Microsoft or used to train AI models. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- The page recommends plugging in a Copilot+ PC to complete initial search indexing. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- The page says Advanced Query Syntax filters work most reliably in the File Explorer search box. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- Searching from This PC checks every drive and is slower than searching from a specific folder. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- The page states that Home in Windows 11 can search across the PC and the cloud. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- Enhanced indexing searches everything on the computer and uses a larger indexing database and more system resources; the default search covers known folders such as Documents, Pictures, and Music. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11), T4)
- Semantic Indexing is described as still in preview and requires an NPU; it is available only on Copilot+ PCs. The article says Microsoft is testing it in File Explorer, Start menu, and Settings. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If nothing matches in a folder, the page recommends expanding the search by going up to This PC and running it again. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 guidance says to select This PC to search all devices and drives, or Documents to search only files stored there. The Windows 11 guidance instead describes searching from Home, a drive, or a folder. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- The page gives the Windows 10 indexing-settings path as Settings > Search > Searching Windows. It states no Windows 10-specific difference in File Explorer search behavior. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- More Options > General > Privacy > Include account-based insights, recent, favorite, and recommended files ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Privacy & Security > Searching Windows > Advanced indexing options ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- Settings > Privacy & security > Searching Windows ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/find-your-files-and-apps-in-windows), T1)
- Advanced indexing options > Modify ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-find-and-use-windows-search-in-windows-10-and-11.html), T4)
- Settings > Privacy & security > Searching Windows > Find my files ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/how-to-boost-search-efficiency-on-file-explorer-for-windows-11), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows + E` — Open File Explorer. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- `Ctrl + C` — Copy selected files and folders. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- `Ctrl + V` — Paste copied files and folders into the destination. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- `Ctrl + A` — Select all visible files and subfolders in the source folder. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The conflict prompt appears when a copied file and a destination file have the same name. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- The page says matching subfolder structures merge recursively by default. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- The comparison option may be unavailable for transfers involving Outlook attachments or certain Outlook .msg, .pst, or .ost files, phones, cameras, other shell-provider devices, application Save or Export windows, folders rather than individual files, or a File Explorer or Windows update defect. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- Availability can depend on the source location, file type, shell provider, and current Explorer build. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- For phone or application sources, the article suggests copying the files first to a normal local folder and then copying them to the final destination; this workaround is not guaranteed for every device or provider. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- A destination folder cannot contain two files with identical names; keeping both produces a renamed copy, usually with a numeric suffix. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The question’s author says the two initial suggested methods did not resolve the issue. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- A reply states that the behavior is a Windows 10 design choice and is not caused by Windows 10 versions 1903 or 1909; it suggests sending feedback to Microsoft if a change is desired. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- The page warns that Replace the file in the destination overwrites immediately and should not be selected blindly. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- The page states that Ctrl + Z cannot restore a destination file overwritten by a Replace action. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- The article says that seeing only Replace the file in the destination and Skip this file does not necessarily mean Windows has disabled keep-both globally. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- The article warns that using Do this for all conflicts may result in non-conflicting files being skipped in some reported File Explorer transfers; it recommends resolving important conflicts individually and verifying the destination afterward. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page discusses Windows 10 and mentions versions 1903 and 1909. It provides no Windows 11 or Windows 7 comparison. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- The page says Windows 10 and Windows 11 use the same conflict-resolution engine. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- For copying, Windows 11 uses the top command bar; Windows 10 uses the Home tab on the top ribbon. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/how-to-safely-merge-folders-in-windows-10-and-11-file-explorer-conflict-choices-and-robocopy.449854/), T5)
- Older Windows releases used the labels Copy and Replace, Don’t copy, and Copy, but keep both files. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- Windows 10 and current Windows 11 builds generally use the newer wording; the keep-both behavior is available through Compare info for both files. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)
- The article does not state a Windows 7-specific difference. ([itechguides.com](https://www.itechguides.com/copy-but-keep-both-files-option-missing-in-windows-10-or-11/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- File Explorer > View > Options > Folder Options > Restore Defaults ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- File Explorer > View > Options > Folder Options > View > Restore Defaults ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- File Explorer > View > Options > Folder Options > View > Advanced settings > Hide folder merge conflicts ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)
- File Explorer > View > Options > Folder Options > View > Launch folder windows in a separate process ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/answers/questions/3262350/skip-or-replace-files-dialog-box), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win + R` — Open the Run dialog, according to the AI answer. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5655432/how-do-i-set-up-a-warning-tab-when-i-delete-files), T5)
- `Shift + Delete` — The answer cites this as an example of permanent deletion. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5655432/how-do-i-set-up-a-warning-tab-when-i-delete-files), T5)
- `Win + D` — Shows the desktop. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- `Delete` — Moves eligible files to the Recycle Bin. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- `Win + I` — Opens Settings. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The question author states the device is a new Thinkpad used for less than a week. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/4272766/cannot-delete-to-recycle-bin), T5)
- No region or rollout conditions are stated. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/4272766/cannot-delete-to-recycle-bin), T5)
- Recycle Bin size limits and the option to bypass the bin are configured per drive; the delete confirmation setting applies globally. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Storage Sense cleans C:; it points to Advanced storage settings > Storage used on other drives for other drives. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Storage Sense settings are per-user. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Storage Sense needs the user to be signed in and online for more than 10 minutes to run. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Storage Sense may be enabled temporarily if the drive is critically low on space, and that by default it runs when the storage bar in Settings > System > Storage turns red. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says Shift + Delete does not use the Display delete confirmation dialog setting and has its own confirmation. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says deletions from removable drives and network locations, cloud-only files, and files deleted with the immediate-removal option do not go to the Windows Recycle Bin. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says items older than the configured Storage Sense age can be erased automatically. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says when a drive’s bin fills, Windows permanently removes the oldest items first to make room. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page states that the OneDrive recycle-bin retention periods are 30 days for personal Microsoft accounts and 93 days for work or school accounts unless an administrator changed the latter. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The answer says enabling the checkbox displays a delete confirmation dialog. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4291681/in-windows-11-how-to-you-turn-on-a-dialogue-that-c?forum=windows-all), T5)
- The question author reports that deleting a file prompts for permanent deletion despite “Don't move files to Recycle Bin” being OFF. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/4272766/cannot-delete-to-recycle-bin), T5)
- The question author reports that files deleted this way are not found in Recycle Bin. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/4272766/cannot-delete-to-recycle-bin), T5)
- The accepted answer asks whether the files are being deleted from the C drive or from an external USB drive or flash drive; no response to that question is included. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/4272766/cannot-delete-to-recycle-bin), T5)
- The answer says enabling “Display delete confirmation dialog” prompts before files are sent to the Recycle Bin. ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5655432/how-do-i-set-up-a-warning-tab-when-i-delete-files), T5)
- With Display delete confirmation dialog enabled, ordinary deletions show an “Are you sure you want to move this to the Recycle Bin?” style prompt. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- Shift + Delete has its own confirmation and does not use the delete confirmation setting. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page describes a possible “The Recycle Bin on this drive is corrupted” message and says resetting the affected drive’s $Recycle.Bin folder permanently deletes everything currently in that drive’s bin. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The confirmation prompt asks: “Are you sure you want to move this file to the Recycle Bin?” ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-enable-or-disable-delete-to-recycle-bin-confirmation-dialog-in-windows-11/), T4)
- Files too large for the Recycle Bin have a separate permanent-deletion warning. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-enable-or-disable-delete-to-recycle-bin-confirmation-dialog-in-windows-11/), T4)
- A Group Policy or registry setting can override or lock the Properties checkbox. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-enable-or-disable-delete-to-recycle-bin-confirmation-dialog-in-windows-11/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page says Windows 11 controls desktop system icons through Personalization rather than the old Control Panel applet. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- The page says the default Recycle Bin size formula has been in effect since Windows Vista. ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Personalization > Themes > Related settings > Desktop icon settings ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Storage > Storage Sense ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Storage > Advanced storage settings > Storage used on other drives ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files ([tutorialpedia.org](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/recycle-bin-settings-windows-11/), T4)
- Settings > Personalization > Themes > Desktop icon settings: enable Recycle Bin if its desktop icon is missing. ([geekrewind.com](https://geekrewind.com/how-to-enable-or-disable-delete-to-recycle-bin-confirmation-dialog-in-windows-11/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` — Open Task Manager. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- `Shift + right-click` — Access the classic context menu temporarily. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Not all extensions from Windows 10 are available in the streamlined Windows 11 context menu; they are available when selecting Show more options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- Some apps may update over time to join the new context menu. The page advises checking with the app developer about availability and timing for specific apps. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- The page specifies Windows 11 and says administrator privileges are needed to modify the registry. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- The page recommends backing up the system or exporting the registry before proceeding. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- When applying a .reg file, click Yes at the User Account Control prompt and then click Yes in the Registry Editor prompt. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- If the classic menu does not appear, the page recommends ensuring administrator privileges, checking that the .reg file was applied successfully, and restarting Windows Explorer or rebooting. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- If system issues occur, the page recommends using RevertToWindows11Menu.reg or restoring the registry backup. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- The article advises caution with apps or functions that require a registry edit and says users should understand what they are doing to their PC. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/app-brings-back-windows-10-context-menu-windows-11), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The streamlined Windows 11 context menu differs from the previous Windows 10 context menu: not all Windows 10 extensions are available in the streamlined menu, but they are available through Show more options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/fileexplorer/file-explorer-in-windows), T1)
- The page contrasts the full classic context menu with the simplified Windows 11 menu and says the simplified menu was introduced in Windows 11. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([github.com](https://github.com/ofirbinder/Win11-Classic-Context-Menu), T2)
- The classic context menu is identified as the Windows 10 context menu. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/app-brings-back-windows-10-context-menu-windows-11), T4)
- The article says the Windows 11 menu is shorter and more organized, while some users dislike clicking “Show more options” to perform certain tasks. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/app-brings-back-windows-10-context-menu-windows-11), T4)

| WA.13.16.i04 | Right-click or press and hold a zipped folder, select Extract All..., and follow the instructions. | Extracts all contents of the zipped folder. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files) |
| WA.13.16.i05 | Drag files or folders to a zipped folder created earlier. | Adds them to the zipped folder. | T1 | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files) |
| WA.13.16.i06 | Right-click selected files or a folder; select Compress to and then ZIP file, 7z file, or TAR file. | File Explorer creates the archive in the same folder as the selected source item or items; the source remains unchanged. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/) |
| WA.13.16.i07 | Type a meaningful name if the new archive name is selected for editing, then press Enter. | The archive is named accordingly. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/) |
| WA.13.16.i08 | Right-click a .zip, .7z, or .tar archive and select Extract All…; review the destination, optionally choose Browse, then select Extract. | File Explorer copies the archive contents to the destination and leaves the archive in its original location. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows + E` — Open File Explorer. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- `Ctrl` — Hold while selecting multiple separate files or folders. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- `Windows + I` — Open Settings to check the Windows version. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Windows 11, version 24H2 supports ZIP, RAR, 7z, and TAR archive formats. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files), T1)
- Windows 11, version 24H2 supports compression and decompression of various formats, including 7-Zip. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files), T1)
- Windows 11, version 24H2 does not support operations on encrypted archive files; the page suggests non-Microsoft applications such as 7-zip or WinRAR for creating or decompressing encrypted archives. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files), T1)
- The page warns that encrypted files added to a zipped folder will be unencrypted when unzipped, which might disclose sensitive information, and recommends avoiding zipping encrypted files. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Windows/Experience/Storage-FileManagement/zip-and-unzip-files), T1)
- Windows 11 File Explorer support for creating and extracting ZIP, 7z, and TAR archives requires version 24H2 or later. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- No SKU, hardware, region, or Insider/rollout conditions are stated. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- RAR is not mentioned as a supported format. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- Native archive creation was tested in Windows 11 Build 25992 (Canary) or newer. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2023/11/10/first-look-windows-11-preview-lets-you-create-zip-7z-and-tar-archives-natively/), T4)
- The feature was rolling out to some Windows Insider Program users; Microsoft was initially testing it with Canary Channel users. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2023/11/10/first-look-windows-11-preview-lets-you-create-zip-7z-and-tar-archives-natively/), T4)
- Viewing the listed archive formats requires the latest optional update, KB5031455, according to the article. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2023/11/10/first-look-windows-11-preview-lets-you-create-zip-7z-and-tar-archives-natively/), T4)
- The article says password-protected files cannot currently be compressed or uncompressed. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2023/11/10/first-look-windows-11-preview-lets-you-create-zip-7z-and-tar-archives-natively/), T4)
- Creating .rar archives is not supported. The article says WinRAR clarified that Microsoft would need to pay to add .rar support. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2023/11/10/first-look-windows-11-preview-lets-you-create-zip-7z-and-tar-archives-natively/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- After creation, the archive appears beside the original content and the originals remain unchanged. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- The extraction dialog lets the user review the destination before extracting. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- When extracting into an existing folder, File Explorer may ask whether to replace files in the destination. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- File Explorer does not create password-protected or encrypted ZIP, 7z, or TAR archives and cannot operate on encrypted archive files. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 File Explorer supports creating and extracting ZIP files only; it does not provide native File Explorer controls for 7z or TAR archives. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > About > Windows specifications > Version ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)
- Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/tutorials/extract-and-create-7z-tar-and-zip-archives-with-windows-11-file-explorer.440358/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The feature began rolling out with the September 2025 Security Update and was still rolling out at the time of the article. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- The options were not available to users in Europe, according to the article. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- The article says the steps apply whether the device is a traditional PC or a Copilot+ PC. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- JPG, JPEG, and PNG files are identified as supported image formats for the listed image actions. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- Microsoft 365 document actions require the Microsoft 365 apps to be installed locally. Supported document types listed are XLSX, PPT, PPTX, DOC, DOCX, PDF, TXT, RTF, ASPX, and HTML. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- AI actions are designed for user files such as photos and documents, not folders or system files. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)
- The image actions support .jpg, .jpeg, and .png files. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)
- To see Microsoft 365 file actions, users must be enrolled in the Microsoft 365 Insider Program, and their PC must be on the Beta Channel. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)
- For Summarize, a Microsoft 365 subscription with a Copilot subscription is required; Microsoft account and Microsoft Entra ID are supported. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)
- For Create an FAQ, a commercial Microsoft 365 subscription with a Copilot subscription is required; Microsoft Entra ID is supported. Consumer support with a Microsoft account is described as coming later. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)
- The article says the features are rolling out gradually, including among Insiders. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)
- To enable AI actions manually, the article says to join the Windows Insider Program, enroll the PC in the Dev or Beta Channel, use the latest Dev or Beta build, and use ViVeTool with feature IDs 54792954,55345819. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/windows-11/windows-11-is-getting-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-heres-how-to-try-them-right-now), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > Apps > Actions ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/microsoft/windows-11/how-to-manage-ai-actions-in-file-explorer-on-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The redesigned interface is reported only in Experimental Channel build 26300.8935. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/), T5)
- The page gives no SKU, hardware, or regional requirements. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/), T5)
- The page provides no rollout date or compatibility inventory. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/), T5)
- The new interface was found in Windows 11 Experimental build 26300.8935. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-news.4/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/?amp=1), T5)
- The reported new-interface behavior was limited to an unusual Recycle Bin case; the page does not establish that ordinary files or all types of Properties sheets use it. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-news.4/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/?amp=1), T5)
- Microsoft had not published a rollout date, supported-build list, or public compatibility inventory for the replacement. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-news.4/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/?amp=1), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The existing Windows 11 property sheet is described as a classic tabbed interface whose visual language predates Fluent Design, Mica, and system-wide dark mode. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-news.4/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/?amp=1), T5)
- The page does not state differences from Windows 10 or Windows 7. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/windows-news.4/windows-11-build-26300-8935-tests-recycle-bin-file-properties.442262/?amp=1), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Ctrl + click` — Select multiple individual files in the dialog, if supported by the app. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)
- `Shift + click` — Select a range of files in the dialog, if supported by the app. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)
- `Ctrl + A` — Select all items in the dialog, if supported by the app. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Multi-file selection depends on whether the app allows its Open dialog to accept more than one file. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The default Save dialog options include FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT; the page says the dialog displays a prompt by default when the user chooses to overwrite a file. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- By default, a sharing violation displays an error, leaves the dialog open, and requires another choice. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- Show can return HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_CANCELLED) when the user cancels, or another error such as E_OUTOFMEMORY. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- An application can reject a chosen item in OnFileOk by returning S_FALSE; the dialog then remains open. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- Show can return HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_CANCELLED) when the user cancels. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- Show can return another error code, such as E_OUTOFMEMORY. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- By default, the Save dialog prompts before overwriting a file. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- Check that every file picked stays highlighted before selecting Open. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)
- If only one file stays highlighted, the app accepts a single file; open the others one at a time. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Starting with Windows Vista, the Common Item Dialog supersedes the older Common File Dialog for opening or saving files. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- The page says the older GetOpenFileName and GetSaveFileName APIs do not support the Shell namespace, modern dialog customization, or file metadata features. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- The page describes pre-Windows Vista dialog state as being saved per process and reused regardless of the particular action; Windows Vista introduced dialog-specific GUIDs through SetClientGuid. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- The page does not state Windows 10- or Windows 7-specific differences. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog), T1)
- The older GetOpenFileName and GetSaveFileName functions are legacy and should not be used in new applications. They do not support the Shell namespace, modern dialog customization, or file metadata features. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- Prior to Windows Vista, state such as the last visited folder was saved per process and used regardless of the particular action. Windows Vista allows a GUID to be assigned to a dialog with IFileDialog::SetClientGuid. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- The page says that the newer version is named the Common Item Dialog, but it continues to be called the Common File Dialog in most documentation. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/bb776913(v=vs.85)?view=vs-2019), T1)
- The page says the same dialog selection methods work in Windows 11 and Windows 10; it states no Windows 10-specific difference for this feature. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-select-multiple-files-in-windows-11-and-10-pc.html), T4)
- The article says enabling “Register as shell extension” lets dialog box prompt windows use the Windows 10 ribbon style. ([pcisawesome.com](https://pcisawesome.com/how-to/how-to-make-windows-11-look-like-windows-10/), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- ExplorerPatcher Properties > File Explorer Customization ([pcisawesome.com](https://pcisawesome.com/how-to/how-to-make-windows-11-look-like-windows-10/), T4)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `IFileDialog` | Common base interface for configuring and displaying the dialog, setting options and file types, and retrieving results. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileOpenDialog` | Open-dialog interface; supports multiselect and retrieving multiple results. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileSaveDialog` | Save-dialog interface; supports setting the current item with SetSaveAsItem. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileDialogEvents` | Receives dialog notifications and handles events such as OnFileOk, sharing violations, and overwrite decisions. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileDialogCustomize` | Adds controls and choices to the dialog. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileDialogControlEvents` | Receives events from added controls. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IShellItem and IShellItemArray` | Represent the item or items returned by the dialog; an IShellItem can provide a file-system path or a stream. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileDialog::SetDefaultFolder` | Sets the folder shown the first time the dialog opens from the application. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |
| `IFileDialog::SetFolder` | Forces the dialog to use a folder regardless of the user's previous location. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog) |

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The PSA settings UI is an optional UWP extension contract. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The Windows 11, version 22H2 dialog-integration enhancements are identified as version-specific in the page. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The CPD is not triggered by apps that need to show a print preview; those apps implement their own dialog. The page gives Office apps as an example. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The page identifies MPD with apps using Windows.Graphics.Printing API and CPD with apps using the Win32 API. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The page says apps needing print preview do not trigger CPD and implement a version of the dialog themselves. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The page says print support settings UI activation requires no new capability. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The page says the settings UI app is expected to handle multiple simultaneous activations for different print jobs. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If a PrintTicket is invalid after validation, the sample keeps the settings UI open and shows an error. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The print dialog enhancement sample checks `AllowedCustomFeaturesAndParametersCount`; if the requested features and parameters exceed it, the sample advises reducing their number. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The preview may not show any preview; the page says the preview function is a Microsoft function and is not within the page author’s control. ([support.ocisystem.com](https://support.ocisystem.com/portal/en/kb/articles/windows-10-11-new-print-dialog), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page distinguishes MPD from CPD by the printing API used: Windows.Graphics.Printing displays the MPD, while Win32 displays the CPD. It does not describe Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- The page describes the new print dialog for Windows 10 and 11 and says the old style can be selected by setting PreferLegacyPrintDialog to 1. It does not mention Windows 7. ([support.ocisystem.com](https://support.ocisystem.com/portal/en/kb/articles/windows-10-11-new-print-dialog), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Preferências de Impressão in the Settings app ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- Printing Preferences in the Settings app can invoke the PSA settings UI. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide), T1)
- Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Print\UnifiedPrintDialog ([support.ocisystem.com](https://support.ocisystem.com/portal/en/kb/articles/windows-10-11-new-print-dialog), T4)

Developer APIs and configuration surfaces (API, not user UI):

| API / element | Purpose as documented | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `windows.printSupportSettingsUI` | Invokes the PSA settings UI from Mais Configurações in the MPD, Preferências in the CPD, or Preferências de Impressão in Settings. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| `PrintSupportExtensionSession.PrinterSelected` | Notifies the PSA when the associated printer is selected in the print dialog; the PSA can provide an Adaptive Card and request custom features and parameters. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-pt/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``windows.printSupportSettingsUI`` | UAP extension contract invoked from More Settings in MPD, Preferences in CPD, or Printing Preferences in Settings. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``ActivationKind.PrintSupportSettingsUI`` | Activation kind received by apps activated with the settings UI contract. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``PrintSupportSettingsUISession`` | Provided on settings UI activation; can be used to get the current `PrintTicket` and `PrintDevice` objects. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``PrintTicket`` | Represents print-related features and values; the settings UI app may modify and validate it. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``PrintDevice`` | Can be used to communicate with the printer to receive printer and job attributes. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``PrintSupportPrintTicketTarget`` | The page says the app submits the modified print ticket using this object. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``SupportsMultipleInstances`` | Manifest element the page says the PSA must support for multiple simultaneous settings UI activations; failure might result in confirming one print job's preferences closing other open preferences windows. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``PrintSupportPrinterSelectedEventArgs`` | Used by the `PrinterSelected` callback in the print dialog enhancement example; the sample uses it to set an AdaptiveCard and request additional features and parameters. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``SetAdaptiveCard`` | Shows an AdaptiveCard in the print dialog in the enhancement example. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``SetAdditionalFeatures`` | Requests additional features to be shown in the print dialog. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``SetAdditionalParameter`` | Requests an additional parameter to be shown in the print dialog. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``AllowedCustomFeaturesAndParametersCount`` | Provides the count limit checked by the print dialog enhancement example before requesting additional features and parameters. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |
| ``AppInfo`` | The print dialog enhancement scenario can get the `Windows.ApplicationModel.AppInfo` of the printing app. | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devapps/print-support-app-design-guide) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win + H` — Opens the Share sheet, according to the page. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The OneDrive options described apply when OneDrive files are saved on the PC. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- Email a contact requires a desktop mail app to be installed. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- Nearby sharing works across Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- Windows Share is enabled automatically and is always available in in-box apps such as File Explorer. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/books/windows-11-field-guide/files/339934/share), T4)
- The Resolution drop-down and Edit button appear when sharing a compatible image file. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/books/windows-11-field-guide/files/339934/share), T4)
- Phones appear as targets if they have been configured with Phone Link. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/books/windows-11-field-guide/files/339934/share), T4)
- Nearby sharing can share with another PC on the same local network or with a PC paired through Bluetooth. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/books/windows-11-field-guide/files/339934/share), T4)
- Apps listed under Sharing using depend on which apps are installed and compatible with the item being shared. ([thurrott.com](https://www.thurrott.com/books/windows-11-field-guide/files/339934/share), T4)
- The source app must support the Windows Share contract for the Share sheet to appear. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)
- An app must register as a share target to be listed as a recipient. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)
- An app may not appear, or content may fail to transfer, if it does not support the relevant sharing protocols or content format. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The page describes `DataPackage.ShareCompleted` as an optional signal that sharing completed and `DataPackage.ShareCanceled` as an optional signal that the user canceled. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/integrate-sharesheet-send), T1)
- For PWAs, the example ignores an `AbortError` and logs other share failures. The page does not describe a Share Sheet confirmation or error dialog. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/integrate-sharesheet-send), T1)
- If the Share sheet does not appear or apps are missing, the page suggests restarting the Windows Explorer process or checking for app updates. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)
- The page says resetting the Share sheet cache through the Settings app may resolve persistent glitches, but gives no specific Settings path. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10 instructions use the Share tab and Share command. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- For Windows 10 OneDrive files, the page describes right-clicking and selecting Share a OneDrive link or More OneDrive sharing options > Invite people; the OneDrive for Business flow uses Share, Copy Link, and Copy. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- Windows 10 also has a workgroup or domain flow: Share tab > Share with > Specific people. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/share-files-in-windows), T1)
- The page says sharing in previous Windows versions, including the Windows 10 era, was often fragmented, with different apps requiring their own export functions; it describes Windows 11 as centralizing the process. ([9to5windows.com](https://9to5windows.com/windows-11-sharing-guide/), T1)

Its `GetForWindow` method obtains a `DataTransferManager` for a window, and `ShowShareUI | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/windows-integration/integrate-sharesheet-send) |

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page describes Windows 7. It says IFileDialog-related interfaces replaced the common file dialog functions used in earlier Windows versions. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/windows/win32/shell/library-be-library-aware), T1)
- Earlier common file dialog functions remain supported in Windows 7, but do not provide the complete Windows 7 user experience and do not support libraries. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/windows/win32/shell/library-be-library-aware), T1)
- IFileOpenDialog is preferred over SHBrowseForFolder because it supports the Windows 7 user interface. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/windows/win32/shell/library-be-library-aware), T1)
- The modern picker is described as a Vista-style file dialog with a navigation pane, breadcrumb bar, and search. ([powershellgallery.com](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/PsUi/1.0.3/Content/public%5Cdialogs%5CShow-UiFolderPicker.ps1), T4)
- The Simple option uses the legacy XP-style tree-view picker instead of the modern picker. ([powershellgallery.com](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/PsUi/1.0.3/Content/public%5Cdialogs%5CShow-UiFolderPicker.ps1), T4)
- No Windows 10 or Windows 7 differences are stated. ([powershellgallery.com](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/PsUi/1.0.3/Content/public%5Cdialogs%5CShow-UiFolderPicker.ps1), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- SettingsIdentifier is used to save and restore the state of the folder picker. ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-app-sdk/api/winrt/microsoft.windows.storage.pickers.folderpicker?view=windows-app-sdk-1.8), T1)
