Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + V` — Opens clipboard history; when used for the first time, it provides the Turn on option. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- `Windows key + V` — Open Clipboard history. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- `Ctrl+C` — Copy the selected item to the clipboard. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- `Ctrl+V` — Paste the most recent clipboard item. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- `Win + V` — Opens the clipboard history flyout; if the feature is off, it lets the user turn it on. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- `Ctrl + V` — Pastes the selected clipboard-history item after it has been returned to the active clipboard. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- `Ctrl + Shift + V` — May paste plain text in some apps; app-dependent. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The sync feature is tied to a Microsoft account or work account; use the same login information on all devices. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- Clipboard history is cleared each time the PC restarts, except for pinned items. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- Clipboard history is limited to 25 copied entries; older unpinned items are removed to make room for new items. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- The size limit is 4 MB per item. Text, HTML, and Bitmap file formats are supported. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- Cross-device sync requires signing in on devices with the same Microsoft account or work account; the page also describes the same login information requirement. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- The page describes cross-device sync as applying to supported clipboard text. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- No SKU, hardware, region, Insider, or rollout restrictions are stated. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- Cross-device sync requires signing in to Windows with a Microsoft account; the devices must use the same account. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- Administrators may disable clipboard history or restrict clipboard sync through Group Policy or Intune. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- Android clipboard sharing may use Microsoft SwiftKey or, on many Samsung phones, Phone Link / Link to Windows; availability and reliability vary by device and build. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- The page states a limit of 25 recent clips and an approximate 4 MB per-item size cap. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- Unpinned items are cleared when the PC restarts; pinned items survive restarts. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If clipboard history is not visible, make sure it has been turned on using Windows logo key + V and Turn on. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- If clipboard items do not sync, check that Clipboard history across your devices is On and that the same Microsoft or work account is used on all devices. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- The page states that pinned items are excluded from clearing and survive the described restart behavior. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- The page describes Clipboard history as a recent-history panel, not a long-term archive. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- If Win + V does not open clipboard history, confirm the feature is enabled at Settings > System > Clipboard and check whether organization policies disable it. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- The page suggests restarting Windows Explorer via Task Manager to refresh UI components if the flyout does not open. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- Items may disappear after a restart if they are unpinned, when the 25-item limit is exceeded, or if an item is larger than approximately 4 MB. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)
- If sync does not work, ensure devices use the same Microsoft account; for phone sharing, check the applicable SwiftKey or Link to Windows settings. The page also suggests toggling sync off and on or signing out and back in. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 instructions call the sync toggle Sync across devices; the Windows 11 instructions call it Clipboard history across your devices. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- The Windows 10 instructions state that syncing across Windows 10 devices requires the latest Windows 10 update. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- The page contrasts Clipboard history with the old single-slot clipboard: copying something new replaced the previous item, and the ordinary clipboard vanished on restart. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- The page states that Microsoft documents Clipboard history as a supported feature on Windows 11 and Windows 10, and notes that Windows 10 support ended on October 14, 2025. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- No Windows 7 difference is stated. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Start > Settings > System > Clipboard ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/using-the-clipboard), T1)
- Settings > System > Clipboard ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/), T5)
- Settings > System > Clipboard > Sync across devices ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-history-win-v-tips-pinning-and-cross-device-sync.400906/), T5)

|---|---|---|

| `CanIncludeInClipboardHistory` | A documented clipboard format mechanism for excluding content from Clipboard history. | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/) |
| `CanUploadToCloudClipboard` | A documented clipboard format mechanism for excluding content from cloud clipboard sync. | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-clipboard-pinning-sync-policy-and-retention-risks.436249/) |

### WA.15.02 Snipping Tool and Print Screen

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | PARTIAL — 1 T1/T2 and 2 T4/T5 sources relevant. Official sources are not specific to build 26300.9711; live-build check pending. |
| Applies to (as stated by sources) | Windows 11 (not build-specific); Windows 11 and Windows 10. Windows 11 details are not build-specific.; Windows 11; the policy was observed in Build 26300. The page also discusses Windows 11 24H |
| Relevant sources | [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots) (T1), [uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11) (T4), [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/) (T4) |
| Inspected, not relevant | 0 |
| Snippet-only candidates | 9 (register only) |

Entry points:

- Select Start, search for snipping tool, then select Snipping Tool from the results. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots)
- Press Windows logo key + Shift + S to open the snipping tool overlay for an image snapshot. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots)
- Press Windows logo key + Shift + R to open the snipping tool overlay for a video clip. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots)
- Press Print Screen (PrtSc) for a static image snapshot of the entire screen and place it in the clipboard. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots)
- In the taskbar search box, type snipping tool to find the app and its available actions. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots)
- Press PrtScn; in Windows 11 this opens the Snipping Tool by default. — [uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11)
- Press Windows Key-Shift-S to open the screenshot selection toolbar. — [uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11)
- Search for Snipping in Start and open the program window to access the delay timer. — [uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11)
- Double-click the Surface Pen eraser button to open the Snipping Tool. — [uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11)
- Group Policy Editor: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > File Explorer — [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/)
- Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard (the previously available toggle is no longer shown on Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2) — [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + Shift + S` — Open the snipping tool overlay to capture an image snapshot. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Windows logo key + Shift + R` — Open the snipping tool overlay to capture a video clip. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Print Screen (PrtSc)` — Capture a static image snapshot of the entire screen and place it in the clipboard. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Alt + M` — Choose a snipping mode. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Alt + N` — Create a new snip in the same mode as the last one. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Shift + arrow keys` — Move the cursor to select from different types of snips. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Alt + D` — Delay capture by 1–5 seconds. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Ctrl + C` — Copy the snip to the clipboard. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Ctrl + S` — Save the snip. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `Windows logo key + R` — Open the Run dialog; the page says to type "downloads" there to access the separately downloaded audio file. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- `PrtScn` — By default, opens the Snipping Tool in Windows 11; if that setting is off, copies the full screen to the clipboard. With the stated OneDrive option enabled, it also saves a screenshot to OneDrive. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- `Alt-PrtScn` — Copies the current window to the clipboard. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows Key-Shift-S` — Opens the Snipping Tool screenshot selection toolbar. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows Key-PrtScn` — Briefly dims the screen, saves a PNG to Pictures > Screenshots by default, and also copies the image to the clipboard. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- `Windows Key-V` — Opens Clipboard History, where the last few screenshots are available if Clipboard History is enabled. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- `Print key` — Opens Snipping Tool or the built-in screen-capture interface on most PCs. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Perfect Screenshot is stated to be available only on a Windows 11 AI + PC and only on a Copilot+ PC. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- Color picker is stated to be available only on a Windows 11 AI + PC and only on a Copilot+ PC. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- The page states that all text recognition processes for Text actions are performed locally on the device. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- The article states that Perfect Screenshot and Click To Do are available if the device is a Copilot+ PC. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- HDR screenshot color correction is described for an HDR display when sharing with users of SDR displays. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- Double-clicking the Surface Pen eraser button requires a Surface Pen. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- The article says screenshots can be set to save immediately to Pictures > Screenshots; this can be changed in Snipping Tool Settings. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- The article describes the Surface Pro 4 and newer volume-up plus power-button screenshot method, but that method is outside the Snipping Tool and Print Screen controls. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- Group Policy Editor requires Windows 11 Pro, according to the page. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)
- The policy was observed in Build 26300 and is described as rolling out to users. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)
- The article reports that a reboot is needed for policy changes to fully apply. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The screenshot notification appears in the lower-right corner after capture. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- The article notes that Windows 11 window screenshots may have squared-off corners even when the window has rounded corners. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- The page says Snipping Tool still points users to Accessibility settings to change the Print Screen shortcut, although the referenced setting is absent on Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page also applies to Windows 10 and includes an earlier-version workflow: it labels the mode selector Mode, describes a Save Snip button, and gives File > Print for printing. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- For capturing a menu in the earlier-version instructions, open the menu and press Ctrl + PrtSc; then choose Mode (or, in earlier versions of Windows, the arrow next to New), select a snip type, and capture the area. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- The earlier-version instructions describe opening Snipping Tool with Start search, Windows logo key + Shift + S, or Print Screen. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- Windows 11 combines functionality from Windows 10's Snip & Sketch tool with the newer Snipping Tool. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- The article says the Windows 11 Print Screen key opens the Snipping Tool by default; turning off Use the Print screen key to open screen capture restores the traditional behavior of copying the full screen to the clipboard. ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- See More > Settings: change automatic save behavior or the default Screenshots folder. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots), T1)
- Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard > Use the Print screen key to open screen capture ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- Snipping Tool > three-dot menu > Settings ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- OneDrive taskbar cloud icon > Settings > Backup > Save Screenshots I capture to OneDrive ([uk.pcmag.com](https://uk.pcmag.com/migrated-3765-windows-10/136730/7-screenshot-features-windows-11), T4)
- Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > File Explorer ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)
- Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard ([windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/03/02/microsoft-finally-gives-you-greater-control-over-print-screen-key-in-windows-11-including-access-to-third-party-apps/), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows key + . (period)` — Opens the emoji keyboard during text entry. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/windows-keyboard-tips-and-tricks), T1)
- `Windows key + ; (semicolon)` — Opens the same emoji panel. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- `Tab / Shift + Tab` — Moves between emoji categories. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- `Arrow keys` — Moves between emoji or highlights a result. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- `Enter` — Inserts the highlighted emoji. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- `Esc` — Closes the panel. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- `Windows key + Period` — Opens the panel. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- `Windows key + Semicolon` — Alternative shortcut for opening the panel. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- `Tab` — Moves among panel search and category controls. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- `Left Arrow and Right Arrow` — Move among Emoji, GIF, Kaomoji, Symbols, and Clipboard history. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The keyboard shortcut requires a text field to have focus. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- The touch keyboard opens automatically when a text field is tapped in tablet use; on a laptop, the Touch keyboard icon may need to be enabled. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Emoji search is stated to work in more than 150 languages. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Support for Emoji 17.0 reached Windows 11 Insider builds in September 2026 and arrives through Windows updates. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- The page states that Windows 11 switched its GIF provider to GIPHY from the June 23, 2026 update (KB5095093) onward. It says Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H1 need that update or later for GIF service availability. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Panel tabs and controls can vary by Windows version, build, region, policy, and rollout status. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- The Emoji and more taskbar control is not available uniformly; feature rollouts, Insider channels, device capabilities, language settings, managed policies, and installed updates can affect whether it is present or active. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- The touch keyboard route is particularly relevant to tablets and convertible PCs; automatic opening is described for supported text fields on touchscreens. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- The GIF section depends on an online service, network access, and current Windows components. The page says Windows 11 updates released starting June 23, 2026 delivered the GIPHY transition and advises installing the latest update by June 30, 2026 to retain GIF functionality. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- Password fields, secure prompts, elevated windows, remote sessions, games, legacy software, and custom text controls may ignore the shortcut or reject the inserted Unicode character. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- The page does not state a Copilot+ PC requirement. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- The panel opens at the text cursor when a text field has focus. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- If Windows key + . does nothing, the page suggests clicking in a text field or trying Windows key + ;. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- If the GIF service is unavailable, the page suggests installing Windows updates, including KB5095093 or later, and restarting. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- An emoji may appear as an empty box or letters if the app or font cannot render it. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- If the shortcut appears unresponsive, test it in a normal editable text field and try the alternative shortcut. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- An unupdated machine may show a message that the GIF service is unavailable while ordinary emoji insertion continues to work. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- If the taskbar control is missing, greyed out, or unreliable, the page recommends the keyboard shortcut as a fallback and advises against unofficial Registry modifications as the first response. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10: The page also states that Windows key + . (period) opens the emoji keyboard during text entry, where users can select or search for emojis. It does not state the Windows 11 GIFs, Kaomoji, or Symbols details for Windows 10. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/windows-keyboard-tips-and-tricks), T1)
- Windows 7 differences are not stated. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/windows-keyboard-tips-and-tricks), T1)
- Windows 10 uses the same Windows key + . and Windows key + ; shortcuts. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Windows 10 has emoji categories but no GIFs tab. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Windows 10 received kaomoji and symbol sections in 2019 and later updates. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- On older Windows 10 builds, typing to search filters only the emoji section, not kaomoji or symbols. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Windows 10 touch keyboard access uses the taskbar option Show touch keyboard button; the page gives Windows 11's setting as Taskbar settings > System tray icons > Touch keyboard > Always. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- The page does not state Windows 7 differences. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- The core emoji shortcut works in both Windows 10 and Windows 11. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- Windows 10 machines retain the panel after free consumer support ended on October 14, 2025, but the page describes it as a legacy feature rather than an actively evolving service. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- Windows 11 is the supported platform for ongoing panel improvements, service changes, and reliability fixes. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- The page states that applicable extended-support programs may provide organizations additional operating-system updates, but do not necessarily guarantee every newer Windows 11 expressive-input capability. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)

Related Settings paths:

- Taskbar settings > System tray icons > Touch keyboard > Always ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Start > Settings > Windows Update ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-on-windows-1011.html), T4)
- Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > system-tray controls > Emoji and more ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)
- Taskbar right-click > Taskbar settings > System tray icons > Touch keyboard ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/windows-11-emoji-panel-open-it-with-win-period-in-2026.439696/), T5)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Win + I` — Opens Windows Settings. ([support.getcleartouch.com](https://support.getcleartouch.com/portal/en/kb/articles/enabling-and-using-touch-screen-keyboard-in-windows-11), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- The page describes the touch keyboard for a Windows device with a touchscreen. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- Split keyboard and Small keyboard are not available in all languages. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- Swipe-based typing like shape writing is not available in all languages. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- The 12-key layout and 50-on layout are Japanese-only. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- The page describes use on a Clear Touch panel with an integrated PC Module or an external PC connected via HDMI and USB Touch cable. ([support.getcleartouch.com](https://support.getcleartouch.com/portal/en/kb/articles/enabling-and-using-touch-screen-keyboard-in-windows-11), T4)
- Automatic appearance is described when a typing field is clicked and the PC senses no physical keyboard is attached. ([support.getcleartouch.com](https://support.getcleartouch.com/portal/en/kb/articles/enabling-and-using-touch-screen-keyboard-in-windows-11), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The Windows 10 section lists Standard keyboard, Narrow layout (one-handed) keyboard, Split keyboard, Handwriting panel, and Expanded standard keyboard instead of the Windows 11 layout list. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- In the Windows 10 section, Keyboard settings is at the upper-left corner of the touch keyboard; docking and undocking is done by selecting the icons below the keyboard layout options. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- The Windows 10 section describes the Narrow layout (one-handed) keyboard as phone-like and supporting swipe-based typing. It describes Standard keyboard as lacking keys such as numbers or ESC. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)

([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- Start > Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Pen & Windows Ink > Handwriting > Write with your fingertip ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/get-to-know-the-touch-keyboard), T1)
- Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar corner icons > Touch keyboard ([support.getcleartouch.com](https://support.getcleartouch.com/portal/en/kb/articles/enabling-and-using-touch-screen-keyboard-in-windows-11), T4)

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key + H` — Starts voice typing when the cursor is in a text box. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/voice-access/voice-access-frequently-asked-questions-faqs), T1)
- `Windows key + H` — Opens voice typing; using it again stops the microphone. ([education.nsw.gov.au](https://education.nsw.gov.au/teaching-and-learning/technology-for-learning/resources/professional-learning-resources/inclusive-and-assistive-technology/microsoft/speech-recognition-windows11), T4)
- `Windows+H` — Open Voice Typing; press again to start or stop dictation. ([computerworld.com](https://www.computerworld.com/article/3496377/windows-voice-commands.html), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Voice typing can only be started if the cursor is in a text box. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/voice-access/voice-access-frequently-asked-questions-faqs), T1)
- Voice typing offers a number of languages; the page does not list them. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/voice-access/voice-access-frequently-asked-questions-faqs), T1)
- Dictation requires being in a space that requires text. ([education.nsw.gov.au](https://education.nsw.gov.au/teaching-and-learning/technology-for-learning/resources/professional-learning-resources/inclusive-and-assistive-technology/microsoft/speech-recognition-windows11), T4)
- No SKU, hardware, region, or Insider/rollout limitations are stated. ([education.nsw.gov.au](https://education.nsw.gov.au/teaching-and-learning/technology-for-learning/resources/professional-learning-resources/inclusive-and-assistive-technology/microsoft/speech-recognition-windows11), T4)
- Requires an internet connection. ([computerworld.com](https://www.computerworld.com/article/3496377/windows-voice-commands.html), T4)
- A touch-screen device can start Voice Typing by tapping the microphone on the touch keyboard. ([computerworld.com](https://www.computerworld.com/article/3496377/windows-voice-commands.html), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Voice typing is available in Windows 10 as well as Windows 11. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/voice-access/voice-access-frequently-asked-questions-faqs), T1)
- Windows 10 uses Windows Dictation, an older version of Voice Typing; it also requires an internet connection. ([computerworld.com](https://www.computerworld.com/article/3496377/windows-voice-commands.html), T4)
- The Automatic punctuation option does not appear to be present on Windows 10. ([computerworld.com](https://www.computerworld.com/article/3496377/windows-voice-commands.html), T4)

Related Settings paths:

- Settings > System > About: the transcript says this is an alternative way to check the operating system. ([education.nsw.gov.au](https://education.nsw.gov.au/teaching-and-learning/technology-for-learning/resources/professional-learning-resources/inclusive-and-assistive-technology/microsoft/speech-recognition-windows11), T4)
- Taskbar settings > Touch keyboard: select “always” to show the keyboard icon. ([education.nsw.gov.au](https://education.nsw.gov.au/teaching-and-learning/technology-for-learning/resources/professional-learning-resources/inclusive-and-assistive-technology/microsoft/speech-recognition-windows11), T4)

Entry points:

- Press the Windows logo key and Enter. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-windows-app-support-tools)
- Alternatively, press the Windows logo key+R. — [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-windows-app-support-tools)
- Press Windows key + R to open the Run dialog box. — [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html)
- If the shortcut is unavailable or does not work, enter the command in Start search. — [techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html)
- Press Windows key + R to open Run. — [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/)
- Right-click Start and choose Run. — [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/)
- Most listed commands can also be typed into Start menu search. — [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/)

| WA.15.06.i18 | In System Configuration, select Services, select Hide all Microsoft services, then Disable all, then Apply; on Startup, select Open Task Manager. | Begins the page's clean-boot procedure; the page then directs disabling enabled startup items and restarting. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i19 | Type `cleanmgr` and press Enter; choose a drive, select cleanup categories, optionally select Clean up system files, choose the drive again, then confirm deleti | Runs Disk Cleanup for the selected categories. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i20 | Type `%temp%` and press Enter; select files to delete and choose Skip for files Windows will not release. | Opens the current user's temporary-files folder and attempts to delete selected files. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i21 | Type `msinfo32` and press Enter; use Export to save the information. | Opens System Information and saves its information to a file. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i22 | Run `msinfo32 /nfo C:\Temp\Test.nfo` or `msinfo32 /report C:\Temp\Test.txt`. | Saves a report in NFO format or plain text, respectively; the destination folder must already exist. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i23 | Run `msinfo32 /computer ComputerName`. | Queries a remote machine if the user has the required WMI permissions. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |
| WA.15.06.i24 | Type `shell:startup` or `shell:common startup` and press Enter. | Opens the per-user or all-users Startup folder, respectively. | T5 | [windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/) |

Shortcuts mentioned by these sources (check against Appendix 3A, which is authoritative):

- `Windows logo key+R` — Opens the Run dialog. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/windows/use-a-screen-reader-to-explore-and-navigate-windows-app-support-tools), T1)
- `Windows key + R` — Open the Run dialog box. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)

Conditions (SKU, hardware, rollout, policy):

- Some tools require administrator rights to change system-wide items; a User Account Control prompt may appear. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- Some Settings pages opened through Run are available only on matching hardware or editions. The page gives battery saver as requiring a battery and Wi-Fi settings as requiring a Wi-Fi adapter. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- Some tasks require an administrator account, particularly clean-boot troubleshooting and full System Information output. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- On managed work PCs, IT policy may block some changes; policy settings might block clean-boot changes on networked computers. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- The all-users Startup folder may require administrator rights. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- A remote System Information query requires the right WMI permissions. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- The destination folder for an `msinfo32` report must already exist. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)

Confirmations, errors and warnings:

- If Windows key + R does not work, use Start search to enter the command. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- To check that a command worked, inspect the new window's title bar, the Settings page heading, or the File Explorer address bar, as applicable. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- The page says to approve the User Account Control prompt if the tool needs administrator rights. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- The page warns that changing advanced boot options in System Configuration without Microsoft support guidance might make the computer unusable. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- After using clean-boot settings, the page says to choose Normal Startup, re-enable services and turn startup apps back on. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- Deleting a previous Windows installation with Disk Cleanup removes `Windows.old` and prevents rollback to the earlier Windows version; the page says the rollback option applies when the upgrade happened fewer than 10 days ago. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- Files in use in the temporary-files folder may not delete; the page says to skip them rather than force deletion. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- In Safe Mode, System Information does not show hardware information, though some system and software details still appear. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- The page says most Windows 10 Run commands still work in Windows 11, but some Settings URIs changed or were removed: ms-settings:backup now opens Sync, and ms-settings:tabletmode was removed. ([techdows.com](https://techdows.com/complete-list-of-windows-11-run-commands.html), T4)
- The page covers both Windows 10 and Windows 11. It says the Windows 10 audio guide reaches the Sound panel through Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Sound, while the Windows 11 guide reaches its Playback and Recording tabs through More sound settings in Settings; `mmsys.cpl` opens the same panel directly. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)
- The page says Windows 11's Settings > Apps > Installed apps is an alternative to Programs and Features, but some apps cannot currently be uninstalled from Settings and Microsoft points users to Control Panel for those. ([windowsforum.com](https://windowsforum.com/news/7-essential-windows-10-and-11-run-commands-for-troubleshooting-cleanup-and-startup.446183/), T5)

- Semantic search in File Explorer and the Windows Search box is stated to be available on Copilot+ PCs. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- The page describes the movable taskbar as a feature Microsoft is adding; it gives no release or rollout details. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)

Windows 10 / 7 differences:

- Windows 10's taskbar is described as having been left-aligned in previous Windows versions; Windows 11 initially centered it and now allows it to be set to the left-hand side. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- Windows 11 redesigned the Start menu and removed Live Tiles, which the page says arguably reduced its functionality. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- Windows 10 has a less customizable News & Information panel; Windows 11 Widgets can integrate with other apps such as Calendar and Spotify. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- Windows 10's Timeline is contrasted with Recall on Copilot+ PCs. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- Windows 11's interface is described as more consistent than Windows 10's, with rounded corners on program windows; some deeper Settings options may still use a dialog box reminiscent of Windows XP. ([pcmag.com](https://www.pcmag.com/comparisons/windows-10-vs-windows-11-how-much-has-microsoft-improved-it), T4)
- Windows 11 places the Start menu and Taskbar in the center; Windows 10 places them on the left. ([cnet.com](https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/every-difference-you-should-care-about-between-windows-10-and-windows-11/), T4)
- No Windows 7 interface differences are stated. ([cnet.com](https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/every-difference-you-should-care-about-between-windows-10-and-windows-11/), T4)

The status column uses each source's own wording (removed, deprecated, changed, new). Wikipedia is a tertiary T4 source that summarises press coverage, so use its rows to locate primary evidence rather than as evidence in their own right.

| ID | Area | Earlier behaviour | Windows 11 behaviour | Status | Source |
